purpose: Consult before defining a glossary term. If a prior published lesson already defines it, adopt that meaning and cross-reference, or declare a glossary `alignment` block that names the prior lesson and the relation (adopt/narrow/extend/distinct-sense/supersede) with a rationale. Never silently redefine a term another lesson owns.

uses.definition: The final severing of the membrane bridge that still joins two daughter cells after the contractile ring has constricted, carried out by the ESCRT-III machinery at the midbody. In cultured human cells it follows anaphase by about an hour and a half. It has its own checkpoint: when chromatin is caught in the bridge, abscission is delayed, which avoids both breaking the DNA and fusing the daughters back into one cell.

The immediate and catastrophic end of a cell exposed to a severe physical, chemical or mechanical insult. No dedicated pathway is involved, so no intervention in the cell's machinery delays it. This is the category that genuinely contrasts with regulated cell death.

A degradative enzyme whose activity is optimal in acid conditions, around pH 4.5 to 5.0 for the lysosomal set. The name records a requirement and not a location: the same enzyme at the cytosolic pH of about 7.2 can do little.

A thin, polar polymer of actin subunits, about 7 nanometres across, with a persistence length of 3 to 17 micrometres so that a single filament is rod-like over about a micrometre and floppy over the height of a cell. Subunits are added preferentially at its barbed or plus end, and myosin motors move along it, so an actin structure can both hold a shape and be pulled on under the cell's control. Cross-linking many filaments into a bundle makes the assembly far stiffer than any one filament.

Movement of a solute against its own electrochemical gradient, which requires free energy from a source other than that gradient. Cells drive it in three ways: coupled carriers spend the downhill movement of a second solute, ATP-driven pumps split ATP, and light-driven pumps use absorbed light. The word active refers to the requirement for outside energy and not specifically to ATP, which is the point most easily lost.

The rule for the probability that at least one of two events occurs: add their separate probabilities and subtract the probability that both occur, so that outcomes lying in both events are counted once rather than twice. The subtraction vanishes when the events are mutually exclusive.

The attachment below the tight junction, built from the transmembrane proteins E-cadherin and nectin with cytoplasmic catenins connected directly to actin, and associated with a belt of actin around the cell. It starts and stabilises contact between neighbouring cells. It holds cells together without sealing the space between them; at an adherens junction the neighbouring membranes stay 15 to 20 nanometres apart.

Any arrangement ensuring that a participant's entry into the study is irrevocably committed before their upcoming assignment can be known by anyone in a position to act on it — commitment first, knowability second — so that who enters which group cannot be steered.

The statement covering the values the null hypothesis excludes. A two-sided alternative allows the quantity to differ from the null value in either direction, which is the form used throughout this lesson; a one-sided alternative allows departure in one direction only and counts the other direction as no evidence at all.

alignment.note: Narrows PREM-SCI-002's general sense of a hypothesis to the specific complementary statement paired with a null in a statistical test. It is defined by what the null leaves out rather than by an explanatory account of its own, so it is a weaker object than the scientific hypothesis PREM-SCI-002 teaches.

uses.definition: Having both a water-attracting and a water-avoiding part in the same molecule. A phospholipid is amphipathic: a phosphate-containing head that water accommodates, and two hydrocarbon tails that it does not.

The correct kinetochore-microtubule configuration, in which the two sister kinetochores are attached to microtubules coming from opposite spindle poles. It produces tension across the sister kinetochores and leaves no kinetochore unattached, which is why the spindle assembly checkpoint permits anaphase. The awkward fact this lesson is built on is that a merotelic attachment produces both of those same conditions while being wrong.

A step at which one activated molecule causes many molecules to be activated, converted or modified, so the number affected grows along the chain. Amplification is a property of individual steps rather than of pathways as a whole, and a pathway can contain a strongly amplifying step while showing a small change in output, when that step sits on the arm removing the response. Gains are also reported in more than one kind of unit: a per-event catalytic tally (molecules consumed per input event) is a different quantity from a ratio of two steady-state levels, and the two cannot be divided into one another. In the canonical Wnt pathway the catalytic steps belong to the kinases that mark beta-catenin for destruction.
The units and records actually included in a particular analysis, which may differ from those initially eligible or enrolled.

The stage of a cell division at which the spindle actually pulls and the chromosomes move apart. Meiosis has two of them: at anaphase I the homologs separate, and at anaphase II the sister chromatids separate.

The ubiquitin ligase that marks securin for destruction, thereby releasing separase and triggering anaphase. It is the target of the spindle assembly checkpoint: while the checkpoint is on, this complex is blocked, so securin survives and the chromatids stay joined. Written APC/C throughout this lesson to keep it apart from the unrelated protein abbreviated APC in PREM-BIO-006.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-006 defines APC as adenomatous polyposis coli, the scaffold of the beta-catenin destruction complex. This lesson's APC/C is an unrelated assembly with a different job; the two share only an abbreviation, and nothing in lesson six's definition is altered. The literature resolves the collision by writing this one APC/C, which this lesson does throughout, and the learner is given the disambiguation in prose where the term first appears: Wnt and colorectal adenomas mean lesson six's protein, anaphase and ubiquitin mean this one.

uses.definition: A way of estimating an MCID by relating each person's observed change on an outcome measure to an independent external standard, the anchor, which is often a patient-reported global judgement of change. The target measure supplies the scale and the anchor identifies a reference category of meaningful change.

A chromosome content that departs from the normal complement, as arises when a division gives one daughter too many copies of a chromosome and the other too few. It is the persistent consequence of a segregation error: a cell cannot repair it the way it repairs a broken strand of DNA. Measured missegregation rates in cultured near-diploid human cells are about 0.025 per cent per chromosome per division; no rate has been established for cells in a human colonic crypt.

An unbalanced chromosome number, in which certain chromosomes no longer come in pairs. A balanced number is euploid. Aneuploidy can arise from a meiotic non-disjunction before an individual exists, or from a mitotic error afterwards, and telling those apart is a question about when rather than about the chromosomes themselves.

Apoptosis triggered by the loss of, or by inappropriate, attachment between a cell and the extracellular matrix. The same execution machinery as any other apoptosis, reached from a different starting condition: the cell finds itself somewhere it should not be. The name is Greek for homelessness. In the human intestinal crypt, integrin receptors are reported to have a central role in controlling it; whether it is what triggers shedding at an intestinal surface is not settled.

A coupled carrier that moves two solutes across a membrane in opposite directions, one downhill and the other uphill. Named here to complete the direction vocabulary; no antiporter is worked through in this lesson.

A large scaffolding protein of the beta-catenin destruction complex, present at about 100 nanomolar in the system where the pathway was quantified. It has two roles in this lesson: it belongs to the complex that marks beta-catenin for destruction, and full-length APC is required for that complex to reorient towards a localised Wnt cue. Damage to it therefore leaves beta-catenin accumulating whether or not Wnt has arrived. The gene encoding it carries the same name.

The face of an epithelial cell that looks onto the lumen. In an intestinal absorptive cell it forms the brush border, carries an unusual lipid composition, and does the barrier and nutrient-uptake work.

The face of an epithelial cell that meets the lumen. In a colonocyte it carries the brush border and is where uptake from the gut contents happens. Its protein complement differs from that of the basolateral surface, and a protein delivered to the wrong one of the two is in the wrong place.

A form of cell death the dying cell carries out itself, using machinery it already contains. The cell condenses, breaks into membrane-bounded fragments that keep its contents inside them, and is cleared by neighbouring or phagocytic cells or shed from an epithelial surface, without provoking an inflammatory response. The word names a programme rather than a degree of injury: a cell running it has been switched on, not overwhelmed. Do not treat it as interchangeable with programmed cell death, which is the wider category it belongs to.

A channel protein that lets water cross a membrane along an osmotic gradient. Aquaporins are one of three routes discussed for water crossing an epithelium, alongside movement carried by cotransporters and movement between cells through the tight junctions; how the total divides between the three is not settled.

One of the three domains of cellular life. Archaeal cells are prokaryotic, in that no membrane envelope encloses their DNA, and phylogenomic evidence places eukaryotes as arising from within this group rather than alongside it.

The sum of all the values divided by how many values there are. It answers what each observation would receive if the total were shared out equally, it carries the same unit as the data, and multiplying it by the number of observations returns the total. Every value enters it at full weight, so a value far out in a tail pulls it toward that tail.
One of the groups being compared in a trial. A trial comparing a new routine against sitting quietly has two arms.
A pattern in which measured values or categories of two variables differ together in a sampled dataset; the pattern alone does not specify why it occurs.
A pattern in which measured values or categories of two variables differ together in a sampled dataset; the pattern alone does not specify why it occurs.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-007 owns this term and this lesson keeps its meaning unchanged. The only thing added here is the display that makes an association visible for two quantitative variables. Causal interpretation of an association remains the earlier lesson's territory, and the scatter scene points the learner back to it.

uses.definition: A pattern in which measured values or categories of two variables differ together in a sampled dataset; the pattern alone does not specify why it occurs. Every measure in this lesson quantifies how large such a pattern is, and none of them turns it into a cause.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning established by PREM-SCI-007: a pattern in which two variables differ together in a sample, with no claim about why. This lesson adds only measurement, giving the pattern a size through the risk difference, risk ratio, and odds ratio, and repeats that the size of an association says nothing about its cause.

uses.definition: Distortion caused when post-entry loss, withdrawal, missing outcomes, or exclusion selects an analysis set in a way related to comparison group and outcome or its predictors.
aliases: bias due to loss to follow-up

uses.definition: Output change divided by input change over a specified interval, with the corresponding output-per-input units.
The property that assignment does not systematically favor one group across repeated randomizations, even though chance imbalance can occur in one realized assignment.

A display with one bar per category, the bar's length encoding a count or measured amount. Because a reader compares bars by comparing lengths, its numerical axis has to start at zero; gaps between the bars mark the categories as separate things.
The quantity acted on by an exponent.

The risk of the outcome in the group that did not receive the intervention, or in the comparison group of an observed contrast. It is the starting point a relative measure divides out and an absolute measure preserves, which is why the same relative change corresponds to different numbers of people at different baselines.

The sheet of extracellular material an epithelium sits on, containing laminins, fibronectin, collagen and other matrix components, which the cells above it grip through integrins. Despite the name it is not a lipid bilayer and is not a membrane in the sense this block has used that word so far; it is secreted matrix, and it lies outside the cell rather than enclosing it.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-004 names the basement membrane inside its basolateral membrane entry, as what the basolateral face looks onto beneath the sheet, without defining it. This lesson gives it its own bounded sense because the basal attachment is part of this outcome. Nothing in the earlier usage is changed. The note that it is not a bilayer is included deliberately, because PREM-BIO-004 owns membrane in the strict two-lipid-molecule sense and the same word is doing a different job in this compound.

uses.definition: The sheet of extracellular material an epithelium sits on, containing laminins, fibronectin, collagen and other matrix components, which the cells above it grip through integrins. Despite the name it is not a lipid bilayer; it is secreted matrix lying outside the cell rather than enclosing it. In this lesson it is the surface whose loss anoikis responds to, which is why the term is repeated rather than assumed.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-007 defines basement membrane for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration, including its warning that the word membrane is doing a different job here from the lipid-bilayer sense PREM-BIO-004 owns. Nothing is narrowed or extended. The entry is repeated rather than assumed because attachment to this specific structure is the survival condition anoikis reports on, and a reader who has forgotten which sheet is meant cannot follow scene 3.

uses.definition: The face of an epithelial cell that looks onto its neighbours and onto the basement membrane beneath the sheet. It carries a different set of lipids and proteins from the apical face of the same cell, and its business is contact with the tissue rather than with the lumen.

The face of an epithelial cell away from the lumen: the base in contact with the material the sheet sits on, together with the sides in contact with neighbouring cells. In a colonocyte it is where absorbed material is handed onward towards the blood.

The protein whose amount carries the Wnt signal inside the cell. It exists in more than one pool, and only one of them matters here: a large, highly stable share is bound to E-cadherin at the membrane and takes no part in canonical Wnt signalling. **Free beta-catenin**, the quantity every figure in this lesson refers to, is the pool neither held inside the destruction complex nor yet phosphorylated; sources also call it free non-phosphorylated beta-catenin, or available beta-catenin. It is made continuously and, without Wnt, destroyed continuously, so its level reports the balance of synthesis against destruction. Free beta-catenin that escapes destruction enters the nucleus and acts with TCF and LEF.
A systematic distortion of a study estimate or conclusion introduced through design, conduct, measurement, analysis, or reporting.

A systematic distortion of a study estimate or conclusion introduced through design, conduct, measurement, analysis, or reporting. It can systematically displace an estimate and its confidence interval without making the interval wider, so a precise threshold comparison can still answer the wrong question.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-008 owns this term and its meaning is kept unchanged here, including the list of routes by which the distortion enters. This lesson adds no new sense and only draws out one consequence that matters for threshold reasoning: bias shifts an interval rather than widening it, so the arithmetic of a threshold comparison gives no warning when the estimate at its centre is displaced.

uses.definition: One of the equal-width intervals a histogram divides a quantitative range into. Bin width is chosen by whoever draws the chart and determines how much of the distribution's shape the picture can show.

The discrete distribution of the number of yes results in a fixed number of trials, when each trial has exactly two mutually exclusive outcomes, the probability of yes is the same on every trial, and the trials are independent. With n trials and probability p it puts the count's mean at np and its standard deviation at the square root of np(1 − p).
The study of the molecules and chemical processes of living systems, including enzymes, membranes, energy use, and biological information.

Which components sit where, what each is joined to, and what each is doing. Organisation is what an emergent property belongs to, and it is the variable that matters: the same components in the same number, unarranged, show none of the properties the arranged population shows.

The structure formed when a replicated chromosome pairs with its replicated homolog during meiosis. A bivalent contains four chromatids: two sister chromatids from each of the two homologs. Some texts call the same four-chromatid structure a tetrad; this lesson uses bivalent throughout.

Withholding knowledge of the assigned condition from people involved in a study, from the moment of allocation until the study ends. Applies separately to participants, providers, data collectors, outcome assessors, and analysts.

Holding the family-wise error rate near a target by testing each of m hypotheses at the target divided by m, so five comparisons intended to give an overall 0.05 are each judged at 0.01. It works, and it is conservative: the stricter threshold lowers the power of every comparison it is applied to.
A stated limit on the sample, setting, time, scale, or conditions to which a question refers.

The dense array of fine projections, around a thousand of them on a mature absorptive cell, that covers the apical surface and multiplies the area available for uptake. Each projection is a microvillus. Under a light microscope the array reads as one fuzzy border, which is where the name comes from. A microvillus is one projection; the brush border is the array of them, so the two are not interchangeable.

The apical specialisation of an absorptive intestinal cell: thousands of finger-like microvilli, each about a micrometre long and about a hundred nanometres across, raising apical surface area roughly thirtyfold. Its membrane is unusually rich in glycolipids, which with cholesterol and sphingomyelin form ordered domains that give it stability against the lumen. A single one of those projections is a microvillus; the brush border is the array and its associated structure, so the two words are not interchangeable.

A short-chain fatty acid made by the bacteria of the colonic lumen from material the host has not digested. It supplies seventy to eighty per cent of a mature colonocyte's energy, oxidised inside that cell's mitochondria.
A conclusion whose causal language, strength, scope, and certainty are limited to what the integrated evidence warrants.

An operation that establishes a relation, under specified conditions, between indications and values supplied by measurement standards with associated uncertainties, then uses that relation to obtain a measurement result.
In this lesson, the adjustment or estimation of model parameters within defensible ranges so model output fits relevant observations according to stated criteria.

alignment.note: Lesson 6 defines calibration as a metrology operation relating an instrument's indications to measurement standards. Here it is model fitting: adjusting parameters so model output matches observations. Different objects (an instrument vs a model), same aim of making outputs trustworthy.

uses.definition: A culminating task in which a learner selects and connects knowledge from several subjects to address an unfamiliar, bounded problem and defend the reasoning.
An observational study that selects cases with an outcome and comparison controls without it from the population that produced the cases, then compares earlier exposure.

One of a family of cysteine proteases that carry out apoptosis. They divide by function into initiators, which respond to the signal that starts the process, and executioners, which do the disassembly. This lesson uses the two functional groups and the two routes that reach them, and treats the individual caspase numbers as a lookup rather than as material to hold.
A variable whose values place each case into a named group, such as blood group or disposition. Its values are labels, whether they are stored as words or as numbers.
A conclusion that an outcome difference is due to a specified exposure, intervention, or assignment rather than to the alternative explanations left by the design.
The explicit comparison of an outcome under one exposure or assignment with the outcome under a stated alternative.
A contrast between outcomes under two or more specified exposure or intervention alternatives for a defined population and period.
A reasoned conclusion about whether changing an exposure would change an outcome, under stated assumptions and conditions.

The ordered sequence a cell passes through in order to divide into two: a long preparatory period called interphase, made up of G1, S phase and G2, followed by a short M phase in which the chromosomes are sorted and the cell is cut in two. The word cycle suggests a fixed circuit run at a fixed speed, and that part of the everyday sense misleads. Progress between phases is driven by cyclin-dependent kinase activity and is conditional on specific physical states being satisfied, so the same cycle can take very different times in two cells of the same type.

The squeezing of a single cell out of an epithelial sheet by its neighbours, which close the gap behind it. PREM-BIO-007 used the word once without defining it, and this is the sense meant. Extrusion is a mechanical removal and is separable from death: a cell may be dead before it goes, or alive as it goes and die afterwards. Crowding of the sheet is one thing that drives it.

The membrane-bounded compartment of a eukaryotic cell that contains its DNA, together with the envelope that encloses it. Everyday English uses nucleus to mean the middle or the core of something; here it means this specific compartment, and a cell can have a middle without having one.

The established framework that cells are the basic living units of plant and animal tissues and that cells within ongoing lineages continue pre-existing cellular lineages rather than appearing from non-cellular material. Tissues may also contain abundant cell-derived extracellular material. Division is the usual lineage-preserving route, but specialised cells can form by other processes such as fusion of pre-existing myoblasts into a skeletal muscle fibre. The lineage principle does not address the origin of the first cells. Established in Berlin in 1838 and 1839 and refined afterwards, cell theory fixed the unit of biological organisation while remaining revisable within its scope.

The basic bounded unit of living tissue that is itself alive and maintains an organised internal state. Cells continue cellular lineages from pre-existing cells, but an individual living cell need not be able to divide: mature skeletal muscle fibres are living cells that do not divide. The everyday senses of the word, a room in a prison, a box in a spreadsheet, or a source of current in a battery, carry none of this biology.

An essentially irreversible arrest of cell proliferation, entered when a cell experiences stress of a kind that could otherwise make it cancerous. The cell stays viable and metabolically active and is not removed. Two cautions on the word. It does not mean an old cell: the triggers are damage and inappropriate signalling, and elapsed time is not the definition. And parts of the intestinal literature use senescent loosely for worn-out surface cells about to be shed, which is the everyday sense and not this one.

For independent observations drawn from the same population with finite mean and variance, the result that the standardized sampling distribution of the mean approaches a normal distribution as sample size grows. The mean's centre at the population mean and variance sigma squared divided by n are exact under those conditions; approximate normal shape is the asymptotic conclusion. The theorem gives no universal finite-sample threshold and says nothing about the shape of individual observations.

The specialised region of a chromosome at which the machinery of segregation grips it. It is where the kinetochore is assembled, and therefore where the spindle's pulling force is applied. One centromere per chromosome means one gripping point per chromosome, which is why an error at a single centromere can affect the whole division.

The constricted region of a chromosome at which its sister chromatids are joined and at which the spindle takes hold to move it. In this lesson the centromere also carries information: a reciprocal exchange between homologs swaps the material beyond the point of exchange, so each chromatid keeps its own centromere, and the parental origin of a centromere is therefore what independent assortment sorts and what a marker can be read back from.

A chloride channel of the apical membrane. Protein kinase A, activated by high cyclic AMP, phosphorylates it and increases chloride secretion into the lumen; water then follows that chloride osmotically. Named here as the route the secretion runs through, in contrast with the coupled absorptive route that raised cyclic AMP leaves alone.

A surveillance mechanism that makes a later step of the cell cycle conditional on an earlier step having been completed correctly. It detects a specific physical state and holds a transition while that state is unsatisfactory. Three features are easy to get wrong. It contains no clock, so it can pass a cell in minutes or hold it for hours depending only on what it detects. It is not a place in the cycle. And it is not absolute: a checkpoint delays rather than permanently blocks, and it can be satisfied by a wrong state that happens to look like the state it tests for.

The physical connection between two homologs produced by a crossover, and the thing that holds the pair together until the first anaphase separates them. A bivalent with no chiasma has nothing holding it, which is why an absence of crossing over leads to chromosomes being missegregated. The plural is chiasmata.

The enterotoxin secreted by Vibrio cholerae, which is not itself invasive. Its catalytic subunit transfers ADP-ribose onto the stimulatory G protein's alpha subunit, disabling that protein's ability to switch itself off, so adenylate cyclase runs without pause and cyclic AMP stays high. The toxin does not kill the cell it acts on, and the epithelium stays structurally intact, which is why absorption remains possible.

A small, rigid, largely water-avoiding molecule with one hydroxyl group, wedged among the hydrocarbon chains of animal membranes, where it can be up to 40 per cent of plasma-membrane lipid. It restricts chain movement in a fluid bilayer and also obstructs crystallisation, so it buffers a membrane against change rather than pushing fluidity in one direction, and it lowers permeability to small water-soluble molecules.

One of the strands of a chromosome that has been replicated. A chromosome that has just been copied consists of two chromatids joined at the centromere and still counts as one chromosome, so a cell can hold 46 chromosomes and 92 chromatids at the same time. Keeping the two counts apart is the commonest difficulty in this material.

One linear DNA molecule together with the proteins packaged with it. This lesson uses only the minimum needed to explain segregation: that the genome is divided among more than twenty such molecules, that each carries one centromere, and that S phase leaves each one as two attached copies. How chromatin is organised, how many copies of each chromosome a cell carries, and what a locus is belong to a separate outcome, PREM-06.02 Chromosomes and genomes, which has no lesson yet and which this lesson defers to rather than anticipating.

The growth of a population of cells descended from one ancestor, because that ancestor acquired an advantage over its neighbours. Normal ageing tissue contains many such expansions at once, most of which never become anything else.

A number stored in place of a category label, such as 1 for female and 2 for male, or 1 to 4 for a four-point rating. The numeral is a filing convenience and carries only whatever the original categories carried.

The proportion of the total variation in the response that the fitted model accounts for, obtained as the regression sum of squares divided by the total sum of squares. With a single predictor it equals the square of the correlation coefficient. It measures how much, and says nothing about whether the fitted shape is right.
The numerical factor multiplying the power of ten in scientific notation.

A ring-shaped protein complex that holds sister chromatids together from S phase until the metaphase-to-anaphase transition. Anaphase happens when the ring is opened by cleavage of its RAD21 subunit. Because that cut cannot be reversed, cohesin is the reason a cell's checking has to happen before anaphase rather than during it.

The asynchronous separation of sister chromatids caused by the spindle's own pulling forces during a prolonged metaphase delay, occurring without separase and with cohesin still present on the separated chromatids. It appeared after a few hours of induced delay in the systems where it was measured. Its significance for this lesson is that waiting, which is the only remedy a checkpoint has, is itself a source of error once it goes on long enough.
An observational study that begins with a defined population or exposure groups and compares subsequent outcomes.

Movement of cells that stay attached to one another throughout, so that a cell's direction is set by its neighbours and by the force transmitted between them, rather than chosen independently. Cells leaving a crypt move this way: velocity aligns with the traction the sheet exerts on the matrix, and cells further along drag those behind. It differs from a single cell crawling in culture, which has a free front edge and can make and break adhesions at will.

A variable at which two arrowheads meet on a path, making it a common effect of two other variables; conditioning or selecting on it can open that otherwise blocked path and induce an association between its causes.

A blind-ended tube of epithelium sunk into the wall of the large intestine, holding roughly 700 cells in the descending colon. Dividing cells sit at its base, their daughters move upward and take on specialised jobs as they go, and worn cells are shed from the surface into the lumen. It is the structure this whole module follows.

The absorptive cell of the colonic epithelium, and the kind of enterocyte that makes up most of that lining. It is polarised, with an apical surface meeting the lumen and a basolateral surface meeting neighbouring cells and the tissue beneath, and it is the running example of this lesson.
The base-10 logarithm, written log in this lesson when the base is otherwise clear.

A property of the assignment mechanism, not of the groups that actually resulted: averaged over every way the chance mechanism could have come out, the groups match. Any single study can still be imbalanced.

A space inside a cell enclosed by membrane, holding conditions that differ from the cytosol and actively maintained against the tendency of those differences to even out. The maintained part is what separates a compartment from a container: stop paying for the difference and it goes, while the membrane is still intact.

Separating activities of a cell into different enclosed spaces so that each can be run and regulated on its own terms. In this lesson the compartment in question is the nucleus, and what it buys is the chance to process and check a transcript before any ribosome reads it.

The division of a cell's interior by membrane into separate compartments. It buys incompatible chemistries running at the same time, local concentrations unlike the cytosol, and a controlled sequence of operations imposed by a fixed order of compartments. It is charged for in membrane, in standing energy, in transport machinery and in an addressing system. It is the idea PREM-BIO-001 called emergence, applied one level below the tissue: the properties belong to the arrangement of parts and to no part alone.

The values of the unknown parameter that a study's data do not argue against at a stated level under the analysis model. Describing an interval this way keeps the statement about the data, preserves the model conditions, and avoids assigning a probability to the parameter.
Two or more proposed explanations or relationships considered as possible answers to the same question.

An event and the event that it does not occur. Together they cover the whole sample space and share no outcome, so their probabilities sum to 1 and the probability of one is one minus the probability of the other.
A signed scalar coefficient describing how much of a vector lies along one chosen coordinate direction.
A unit formed by multiplying, dividing, or exponentiating other units, such as metres per second or square centimetres.
Obtaining a reported computational result from the same input data and documented analysis steps, code, and relevant computational conditions.

A systematic difference in the amount of a substance across space, so that the concentration at one place differs from the concentration at another. In this lesson the gradient runs along the length of a crypt and the quantity that varies is a Wnt protein. The word describes the profile and not its cause: a falling profile can be produced by spreading and breakdown, or by handover between cells combined with dilution, and which of those builds the crypt gradient is unsettled. PREM-BIO-003's proton gradient is a difference of this kind across a membrane rather than along a tissue, and the two are separate cases of the same idea.
A relevant feature of the case, setting, or comparison under which a prediction is expected to hold.

The probability of one event among the outcomes where another event holds, written P(A given B) and equal to the probability that both occur divided by the probability of the conditioning event, which must be greater than zero. Conditioning discards every outcome outside the stated group and rescales what remains, so P(A given B) and P(B given A) are different questions with different answers.
Restricting, stratifying, matching, or statistically adjusting an analysis so comparisons are made within or weighted by values of another variable.

A range computed from sample data by a procedure with a stated conditional success rate, reported as a lower and an upper limit in the units of a defined population quantity. It gives the parameter values that the sample is compatible with under the stated sampling and analysis model, and it says nothing about where any individual observation sits.

The stated conditional success rate of the procedure that produced an interval: the long-run proportion of intervals that would contain the fixed parameter if independent sampling and analysis were repeated under the procedure's assumptions. It is a property of the method, not a feeling of certainty, and it does not repair bias or guarantee generalisation beyond the defined population.

A separate rival factor that varies systematically with the independent variable and could also affect the dependent variable, but is not a consequence on the pathway through which the independent variable produces the response.
For the simple structures in this lesson, a pre-exposure common cause that opens a noncausal path between exposure and outcome.

alignment.note: Extends Lesson 3's design-linked rival factor into the causal-graph account: a pre-exposure common cause opening a noncausal path. The reagent-lot examples of Lesson 3 remain valid instances of this fuller definition.

uses.definition: Distortion of an exposure-outcome comparison by another factor related to both the exposure and the outcome, such that the observed association does not isolate the exposure's effect.

The reasoning error of treating the probability of A given B as though it were the probability of B given A. In screening it turns a test's detection rate into a claim about a patient holding a positive result; in reading a study it turns a probability computed under a hypothesis into a probability of that hypothesis.

The reasoning error of treating the probability of A given B as though it were the probability of B given A. Applied to a test result it turns a probability computed under a hypothesis into a probability of that hypothesis, so that p = 0.029 is misread as a 2.9 per cent chance the null is true or a 97.1 per cent chance the effect is real.

alignment.note: Adopts PREM-STA-004's meaning without change: treating P(A given B) as though it were P(B given A). That lesson established the error with screening tables, where the same test gave 0.269 in one clinic and 0.818 in another while its detection rate stayed fixed. This lesson applies the identical error to a p-value, which is the case PREM-STA-004 explicitly forwarded here, and adds no new sense of the term.

uses.definition: The extent to which contributions from different pieces or lines of evidence are compatible for the specified question after differences in design and scope are considered.
A validity problem in which the measurement operation leaves out important parts of the intended construct.

The degree to which evidence and theory support the proposed interpretation of measurement results for a stated use, including how well the operation represents the intended construct and excludes irrelevant influences.
An idea used to organize related observations, such as alertness or coordination, that is represented through chosen indicators rather than observed directly as a single reading.
A feature outside the intended construct that changes measurement results and can therefore distort the proposed interpretation.

A quantitative variable that admits any value inside a range, so how finely it is reported depends on the instrument rather than on the quantity. Fasting glucose in mg/dL and hours before sleep are examples; rounding such a value to whole units does not make it discrete.

The ring of filamentous actin and myosin II that assembles beneath the plasma membrane at the cell's equator and constricts to draw the membrane inward as a cleavage furrow. Its components are the ones PREM-BIO-007 of this block introduced for microvilli and junctions, put to a third use. Where it assembles is set by the anaphase spindle, through a signalling chain that ends in a zone of active RhoA at the equatorial cortex.
An extra comparison condition included to provide a baseline, known response, or another specific check on interpretation.
A protected route in which data are available only to approved users under stated eligibility, security, and use conditions rather than through unrestricted public release.
Another relevant condition deliberately kept alike across the main comparison so it does not create a systematic rival difference.

A group selected because its members were easy to reach or willing to volunteer, rather than by a chance mechanism giving every member of the sampling frame a known chance of selection. In this lesson it is the standard example of a route that narrows or misdirects who a result is about.
Evidence from a predicted relationship between a measure and another defensible measure of the same or a closely related construct.
A ratio of equal quantities used as a multiplicative factor of one to change unit representation without changing the quantity.

A unitless summary of how tightly two quantitative measurements follow a straight-line pattern, always between −1 and +1, sharing its sign with the slope. It reports linear strength only, so a strong curved relationship can produce a small value and very different scatters can produce the same one.
For a right-triangle acute angle, adjacent divided by hypotenuse; on the unit circle, the horizontal coordinate.
The outcome that would occur for a unit under an alternative exposure or assignment, including an alternative not actually experienced by that unit at that time.

The number of coupling ions a transporter moves for each molecule of its substrate, per transport cycle. Two sodium ions per glucose for SGLT1, one for SGLT2. It is the parameter that sets how far uphill a substrate can be driven: the free-energy budget is directly proportional to it, and because that budget enters through an exponent, the largest attainable concentration ratio varies as the coupling ion's concentration ratio raised to this number.

The value of the reported statistic at which a test switches from not rejecting the null hypothesis to rejecting it. For a two-sided test at a significance level of 0.05 on a difference between means, it sits 1.96 standard errors either side of zero, which for the dinner-timing study is 8.09 mg/dL.
A study that measures exposure and outcome in a defined population at one time or over one brief window.

The condition of a cell being acted on by more than one signalling pathway at once, so that its behaviour is a joint function of several inputs instead of one. In the colonic crypt a cell sits in a Wnt gradient falling from the base, a BMP gradient falling from the top, and a contact-dependent Notch input carried on its neighbours' surfaces. Reading several inputs does not by itself supply more positional information: an input that varies along the same axis is largely a restatement of the first, while an input that is not a function of position can make distinctions the axis cannot.

The reciprocal exchange of segments between two homologs during meiosis, so that beyond the point of exchange the DNA of one homolog's chromatid runs continuously into what was the other's. It does two jobs at once: it makes new combinations within a chromosome, and it physically ties the pair together so that the first division has something to pull against.
An experiment in which each participant receives two or more assigned conditions in a planned order and contributes an outcome under each condition.

One completed reciprocal exchange between homologs, and so one countable event of crossing over. Crossovers are counted per meiotic cell by staining for a protein that gathers at them: measured means are about 49 per cell in human males and about 69 in human females, roughly two and three per chromosome pair. A crossover is a single event, whereas crossing over is the process that produces it.

A protein whose concentration rises and falls through the cell cycle and which must be bound to a cyclin-dependent kinase for that kinase to have any activity. Different cyclins partner different kinases at different points, so which cyclins are currently present is in effect a record of which phase the cell is in. Cyclin D and cyclin E act with their partner kinases in G1; cyclin B partners the kinase that maintains the mitotic state, and its slow destruction during a prolonged mitotic arrest is what eventually lets an arrested cell escape.

An enzyme that drives cell-cycle transitions by adding phosphate to target proteins, and which has no kinase activity at all unless it is tightly bound to a cyclin. This makes it a switch with two independent off positions: remove its cyclin, or leave the cyclin in place and add an inhibitor protein that rearranges the active site. Checkpoints use both routes. A cyclin-dependent kinase is the actuator that moves the cycle forward, which is a different job from the surveillance that decides whether it may fire.

The physical division of one cell into two after its chromosomes have been sorted, carried out by a contractile ring that constricts the cell at its equator and completed by abscission of the membrane bridge that remains. It is a separate operation from mitosis, with its own machinery and its own checkpoint, and it can fail on its own: a cell whose cytokinesis fails is left with two nuclei and twice the normal DNA content, and no checkpoint stops it dividing again.

The interior of a cell outside its nucleus, including the fluid and everything suspended or embedded in it. In a prokaryotic cell the cytoplasm is one continuous space holding the DNA and the ribosomes together.

The set of protein polymers inside a cell that give it shape, hold its parts in place, anchor it to its neighbours and to the material beneath it, and generate movement. Three systems make it up in an animal cell: actin filaments, microtubules and intermediate filaments. The name suggests a rigid frame, and that part of the everyday sense is misleading; these polymers are assembled, disassembled and rebuilt continuously while the cell is working.

The fluid inside a cell but outside its membrane-enclosed compartments, held near pH 7.2. It is the reference condition against which every compartment in this lesson is compared, and it is where a protein stays when nothing directs it elsewhere.
A positive per-interval multiplier below one in a discrete exponential model.

A count of how many numbers in a sample were still free to vary once the quantities already computed from it are held fixed. Comparing two groups of 30 leaves 58, because two group averages were computed from the 60 readings before any spread could be measured, and it is the number that selects a row of the t table.
The response recorded to examine whether it differs across levels of the independent variable.

The attachment below the adherens junction, and the one that does not use actin. Desmosomal cadherins, the desmogleins and desmocollins, reach across to the neighbouring cell; plakoglobin and the plakophilins sit on the cytoplasmic face; and desmoplakin anchors keratin intermediate filaments to the membrane. Its job is mechanical coupling under load, which is why it is wired to the polymer that holds force at higher tensile loads than actin. Like the adherens junction, it adheres without sealing.

The assembly that keeps free beta-catenin scarce in a cell receiving no Wnt. It includes APC, Axin and the kinases CK1A and GSK3B; beta-catenin is drawn in, phosphorylated, then tagged with ubiquitin and destroyed in the proteasome. Wnt binding reduces the rate of that destruction, so the pathway raises its output by interfering with destruction instead of increasing production. How the reduction happens is not settled: some complexes relocate to the membrane while remaining assembled, but the complexes that stay in the cytosol remain active, and saturation of the complex or blocking of the ubiquitin-tagging step are both proposed to account for the rest.
Distortion arising when an outcome is measured, assessed, or adjudicated differently because the assessor knows the assigned condition. Also called ascertainment bias.

One observation minus the mean of its data set, carrying a sign and the unit of the data. The deviations of any data set sum to zero, which is why a spread measure squares them before averaging rather than averaging them directly.
Misclassification whose error mechanism differs according to the status of another variable in the analysis, such as outcome classification differing by exposure group.

The spreading of molecules by random thermal motion, with no motor or flow pushing them. The average of the squared distance covered grows in proportion to time, so the time to cross a distance grows as the square of that distance: ten times further costs a hundred times longer.
A description of a quantity type in terms of base quantity types such as length, time, and mass, independent of a particular unit.
The requirement that quantities added or equated have compatible dimensions; satisfying it is necessary but does not prove a model is correct.
A quotient of compatible like quantities whose units cancel, leaving a pure number suitable as a logarithm argument.

Holding both members of every homologous pair. A diploid human cell carries 46 chromosomes as 23 pairs. Ploidy counts chromosomes and not copies of DNA, so a cell whose chromosomes have just been replicated is still diploid even though it then holds two DNA copies of each chromosome. Somatic cells are diploid and stay diploid through every division they make.
In this lesson's nondegenerate family comparison, a relationship y = kx with fixed nonzero k, in which y/x equals k wherever x is nonzero.

A probability distribution over outcomes that can be listed one by one, such as the whole numbers 0 through 60. Unlike a continuous distribution it gives each individual outcome a probability of its own, so asking for the probability of exactly 49 has a real answer rather than zero.
A quantitative variable that admits only separated values, most often whole counts, so nothing lies between two neighbouring values. Nights recorded and admissions in the past year are examples.
Evidence from a predicted weak or distinct relationship between a measure and measures of different constructs.
An expected observation for which competing hypotheses give different outcomes, allowing evidence to count differently for them.

A quantity that has to be supplied before a named distribution describes anything in particular. A normal distribution takes two: a location parameter, its mean, which places the centre, and a scale parameter, its standard deviation, which sets the spread. A binomial takes the number of trials and the probability of a yes result on one trial.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a model parameter as a model quantity held fixed during one run and free to change between runs. This lesson narrows the word to the quantities that identify one member of a distribution family, so that changing a parameter changes which curve you are using rather than which scenario you are running.

uses.definition: The complete account of which values a variable takes across a set of observations and how often each value, or each interval of values, occurs.

A way of contributing to an MCID estimate from statistical characteristics of scores within a sample, such as the standard deviation of change or the measurement error of the instrument. It describes change relative to variation or measurement error, but by itself cannot establish whether a change matters to the person who has it.
A condition limiting allowed variable values, such as a nonzero denominator or a nonnegative integer count.

In classification, the highest rank above kingdom. Cellular life is divided into three: Bacteria, Archaea and Eucarya. This is a taxonomic sense of the word and is unrelated to the set of inputs on which a function is defined.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-005 and PREM-QNT-007 use domain for the set of inputs on which an expression or a function is defined. Biology uses the same word for the highest rank in classification, above kingdom. The two senses are unconnected, and the lesson says so in prose at the point where the taxonomic sense first appears, so a learner who already holds the mathematical meaning is not left reconciling them.

uses.definition: The set of input or candidate values for which an expression and task are defined.
The set of inputs for which a function is defined in the stated context.
A scalar formed by multiplying corresponding components and adding; it measures directional alignment.

A mutation that confers a selective growth advantage on the cell carrying it. A typical tumour contains two to eight of them. Carrying one is not the same as being a cancer: normal, functioning tissue can carry driver mutations in a large share of its cells, so a driver mutation is necessary for the process and not sufficient for the disease.

The precise contrast a study is intended to estimate. In an open-label trial, the total effect of assignment to an intervention package can include ordinary attention and expectations created by that package; a content-specific effect beyond those features requires a comparator that matches them.

The magnitude of the difference or association a study is trying to detect, stated in the units of the measurement, for example a 9.0 mg/dL difference in mean fasting glucose. In a power calculation it is a quantity named in advance, chosen because a difference that size would be worth finding, and it is not the difference the study went on to observe.

The magnitude of an estimated effect, reported in the units of the outcome, such as 9.0 mg/dL of fasting glucose or 2.0 percentage points of screening attendance. It is the quantity a threshold comparison is made against, and it is the part of a result that a p-value cannot be decomposed back into.

The net driving force on a solute across a membrane, obtained by combining the contribution of its concentration difference with the contribution of the membrane potential acting on its charge. For an uncharged solute only the first contribution exists. For an ion both must be counted, and in the enterocyte of this lesson the voltage contribution is the larger of the two, so a concentration ratio alone understates the driving force on sodium.

In this lesson's bounded tissue-level sense, a property produced by the spatial or temporal organisation of interacting cells that is not a property of one isolated cell. For the epithelial examples here, test whether the stated property is absent from one cell and is lost when the relevant arrangement is disrupted. Continuous epithelial exclusion across an area is emergent in this sense; one cell's boundary and transcellular permeability are not. Other fields use emergence in additional technical senses, so this operational test is not a universal definition.
A question for which observations or measurements can bear on the answer.

The statement that the areas a normal distribution places within one, two and three standard deviations of its mean round to 68.27, 95.45 and 99.73 per cent, usually quoted as about 68, 95 and 99.7 per cent. The underlying areas are defined by the normal cumulative distribution function; these displayed percentages are rounded, belong to the model, and transfer to a dataset only to the extent that a normal distribution describes it.
Answerable or assessable using observations or measurements from the world.

A membrane compartment reaching through much of the cell, held near pH 7.2, which receives proteins carrying a signal sequence while they are still being made and is where their folding begins. The rough form is the part studded with the ribosomes making those proteins.

A sheet of cells covering a surface or lining a cavity, joined to its neighbours so that the sheet is continuous. The colonic epithelium is one cell thick and separates the contents of the gut from the tissue beneath it.
A statement asserting that two expressions are equal.
Equations with the same solution set over the declared domain.

The sterol fungi build into their membranes where animal cells use cholesterol. It does the same structural job and is a different molecule, and that difference is what amphotericin B binds and what makes the drug more toxic to a fungus than to us.

A value computed from a sample and offered as a stand-in for an unknown population quantity. Calling a number an estimate commits you to saying how far off it might be, which is what the standard error is for.

A cell whose DNA is enclosed by a membrane envelope of its own, forming a nucleus. Animals, plants, fungi and protists are built from eukaryotic cells, including the colonic lining cells this module follows. Membership in the group is decided by ancestry rather than by this description of how the cell is built, so the envelope is how the word gets applied and not what the word means.

Any collection of outcomes from a sample space that a question is about, such as "the drawn participant ate late" or "the reading was 140 mg/dL or above". An event either occurs or does not on a given trial.
One coherent group of observations or studies that contributes a particular kind of support to a specified scientific question.
A study in which researchers assign an intervention or exposure and compare outcomes under the assigned conditions.
An analysis developed after patterns or outcomes are inspected, used to generate or refine ideas and reported as exploratory rather than as a test fixed in advance.
The integer in a power of ten that records the number's base-10 scale; a negative exponent indicates a reciprocal power below 1.
The intervention, condition, characteristic, or experience whose relationship with an outcome is being compared.
The intervention, condition, characteristic, or experience whose relationship with an outcome is being studied.

alignment.note: Adopts Lesson 4's meaning: the condition whose relationship with an outcome is under study.

uses.definition: A combination of numbers, variables, and operations that represents a value but does not assert equality.
The degree to which a study's conclusion carries over to people, settings, and conditions outside the study. Also called applicability or generalizability.
Using a fitted or calibrated relationship beyond the conditions or range that supplied its direct evidential support.

Using a fitted relationship beyond the range or conditions that supplied its evidence. The equation returns a number regardless, and a straight line returns increasingly extreme values the further out it is pushed, so the arithmetic completing is no sign that the answer is supported.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defined extrapolation as using a fitted or calibrated relationship beyond the conditions or range that supplied its direct evidential support, and this lesson adopts that meaning without change. What is added is the concrete case: the range of one predictor in one fitted line, and the specific values that line returns outside it.

uses.definition: Protein-mediated movement of a solute down its own electrochemical gradient, requiring no energy source beyond that gradient. It covers all channel proteins and many carrier proteins, so it is not the name of a mechanism but of an energetic category: a channel and a carrier can both be doing it. GLUT2 carrying glucose out of an enterocyte and an aquaporin passing water are both examples. Passive transport is the broader category and not another name for this one: it also covers simple diffusion straight through the bilayer, which needs no protein at all. Every instance of facilitated diffusion is passive; not every passive movement is facilitated.

alignment.note: A narrowing of the diffusion sense PREM-BIO-002 owns, to the case where a membrane protein provides the path while the direction and the driving force still come from the solute's own gradient. The word facilitated marks the protein, not any added energy, which is the distinction this lesson's classification turns on. Passive transport is recorded as an alias because the source establishing the category treats the two names as the same thing.

uses.definition: A recognizable way a model becomes inadequate for its intended use, such as an assumption failing, a boundary being crossed, or output disagreeing materially with evidence.

The probability of at least one Type I error across a whole set of tests. For k independent tests each at level alpha it equals 1 minus (1 minus alpha) raised to the power k, so five comparisons at 0.05 give 0.226. Without the joint dependence structure the exact rate cannot be inferred from k and alpha alone; the general Bonferroni upper bound is the smaller of 1 and k times alpha.

The property of a cytoskeletal polymer whose two ends differ, so that subunits are added preferentially at one of them and motor proteins can tell one end from the other. Actin filaments and microtubules have it; intermediate filaments do not. This is a different sense of the word from the cell polarity earlier lessons in this block used, where a polarised cell is one with distinct apical and basolateral surfaces. A cell can be polarised in that sense while containing filaments that are themselves apolar.

The minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, and maximum of a data set, reported in that order. Together they describe where the middle half sits and how far each side reaches, which a single centre value cannot do. Those distances can warn that the sides differ, but they do not identify distribution shape without a plot or the raw values.

Movement of a lipid from one leaflet of a bilayer to the other, which requires dragging its water-attracting head through the water-avoiding interior. Spontaneous flip-flop is rare, less than once a month per molecule in synthetic bilayers, and an established difference between the leaflets takes days to run down without enzymes.

A P4-ATPase that spends ATP to move specific phospholipids, phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine among them, from the outer leaflet to the cytoplasmic one. Flippases are what establish and maintain lipid asymmetry. A floppase is a different transporter, not another name for this one: it spends ATP to move lipids the opposite way, out to the outer leaflet, and generally belongs to the ABC transporter family.

The account of membrane structure set out in 1971 to 1972, in which proteins sit within and upon a fluid lipid bilayer and components diffuse within the plane. Mosaic never implied that components are evenly spread; uneven distribution within membranes was already being observed in the 1960s.

A table listing each category or bin beside the number of observations in it, and often beside that count as a proportion of the total. It reports exact values that a chart of the same data can only be read to the nearest gridline.
The number of observations falling in a given category or bin.

Describes the family of statistical methods, confidence intervals among them, whose statements are read as frequencies across imagined repeats of the same study. A frequentist method reports how often a procedure would behave in a given way and never attaches a probability to the fixed parameter itself.

The receptor that binds Wnt ligands, working together with LRP5/6. Its chain crosses the membrane seven times, and it carries an extracellular cysteine-rich domain, a hydrophilic linker, the seven-transmembrane domain, and an intracellular carboxy-terminal region. Frizzleds are assigned to class F of the G-protein-coupled receptors and were grouped in the IUPHAR database as class FZD within that superfamily. Whether they should be classified strictly as G-protein-coupled receptors is disputed, and this lesson reports the dispute without resolving it.
An operation that uses the output of one function as the input of another.
A systematic change to function inputs or outputs that translates, reflects, or stretches its graph.
A rule or relation assigning exactly one output to each allowed input.

A cell-surface receptor built around a core of seven transmembrane helices, which form three intracellular and three extracellular loops. Binding on the outside is registered by a separate protein on the inner face of the membrane, so the receptor itself neither conducts ions nor performs the chemistry of the response. Signalling through one is switched off by desensitisation: receptor kinases phosphorylate the ligand-occupied form, arrestin binds, the interaction with the G protein is blocked, and the receptor is taken off the surface by endocytosis. Frizzled is assigned to class F of this group, and whether Frizzleds should be classified strictly as members is disputed in the literature.

A haploid cell whose function is to fuse with another gamete. In humans the two kinds are the sperm cell and the egg cell. Meiosis does not produce gametes directly in either sex: in the male it yields haploid spermatids that differentiate into sperm cells afterwards, and in the female the second division completes only at fertilisation. Gametes are also not the only cells meiosis produces, since the polar bodies discarded in oogenesis are meiotic products too.

The time a cell population takes to double in number under stated conditions. It is a property of an organism and its circumstances together, not of the organism alone: Escherichia coli doubles in about 18 minutes in rich broth and about 52 minutes in a minimal medium.
The study of biological inheritance, variation, genes, and how genetic information contributes to observable traits.

The complete DNA sequence a cell carries, measured in base pairs. A bacterial genome is usually a single circular molecule of a few million base pairs; the human nuclear genome is about three billion base pairs across more than twenty linear chromosomes.
The lineage of cells that leads to gametes. It is the only lineage in which meiosis occurs. Novelty is the germ line's product: new combinations of chromosomes are what it exists to generate.

A low-affinity, high-capacity facilitative glucose carrier of the enterocyte. At low luminal glucose it sits in the basolateral membrane, where it lets glucose leave towards the blood downhill and uncoupled, by facilitated diffusion. At high luminal glucose it is also reported in the brush-border membrane, so one transporter per face is a common condition rather than a rule.

A stack of compartments running from about pH 6.7 at the face receiving cargo from the endoplasmic reticulum to about 6.0 at the face dispatching it. Proteins are modified in a fixed order as they pass through, and the final compartment, the trans-Golgi network, sorts them by destination and packages them into transport vesicles.
A per-interval multiplier greater than one in a discrete exponential model.
The positive time required by an exponential decay model for a quantity to become one half of its reference value.

Holding one member of every homologous pair. A haploid human cell carries 23 chromosomes. Because ploidy counts chromosomes rather than DNA copies, a cell can be haploid and still hold two copies of each chromosome's DNA: that is exactly the state after the first meiotic division, and it is why a second division is needed before the cell is a gamete.

A description of one position on a chromosome, comparing the copies a cell holds there. If the copies read differently in DNA sequence, the cell is heterozygous at that position; if they read the same, it is homozygous. The words describe the comparison at that position and nothing more, saying nothing about a whole chromosome and nothing about any trait. This lesson uses them only at the centromere, where they distinguish two copies that are different homologs from two copies of one homolog.

A display of the distribution of one quantitative variable, built by dividing its range into adjacent equal-width intervals and drawing a bar over each interval whose height is the number of observations falling in it. Its bars touch because the intervals are adjacent slices of one continuous scale.

The homeostatic adjustment of membrane lipid composition that holds membrane viscosity roughly fixed as growth temperature changes, chiefly by varying the proportion of packing-disrupting chains such as unsaturated or branched ones and by varying chain length. The ability is broadly conserved across living things.

The two versions of one chromosome that a person carries, one inherited from each parent. They are very similar in DNA sequence without being identical. The two are partners rather than copies of each other, and that distinction carries most of this lesson: partners are separated at the first meiotic division, copies at the second.

The tendency of water-avoiding molecules in water to cluster together. Water must reorganise into ordered cage-like arrangements around such a molecule, which costs free energy, and the cost falls when the water-avoiding parts group so that fewer water molecules are affected. It is what assembles a bilayer and what holds one together, because no bond joins one lipid to its neighbour.
The side opposite the right angle in a right triangle; it is the triangle's longest side.
A proposed explanation or relationship that leads to expectations evidence can test; developed in the next lesson.
A proposed explanation or relationship from which observable expectations can be derived.
An equation true for every value in its declared domain.
The study of biological defence, including barriers, rapid responses, targeted responses, tolerance, and immune memory.

The value an effect must reach before a particular group would act on it, written on the same axis and in the same units as the effect estimate. It is an input to the reading of a result, supplied by the people accountable for the decision. An estimated minimal clinically important difference may inform it, but an individual-change MCID does not automatically become a service threshold for a between-group effect. Stated openly it can be argued with; left implicit it governs the conclusion anyway.

The rule that which member of one homologous pair goes to a given pole at the first meiotic division is settled independently of every other pair. With 23 pairs it gives a binary choice repeated 23 times, so 2 to the 23, about 8.4 million, distinct patterns of parental origin across the 23 centromeres. That count is exact for what it counts and ignores crossing over entirely.
A pattern in which the main potential errors of one approach differ from and are not caused by the main potential errors of another approach.

Two events whose joint probability equals the product of their separate probabilities, equivalently two events where learning that one occurred leaves the probability of the other unchanged. Independence is a property to be tested against the data or defended as a modelling assumption, never assumed for convenience.
Two sets of values from separate cases, with no case appearing in both and no value in one set tied to a particular value in the other.
In the experiments used in this lesson, the factor deliberately changed between the main comparison conditions.
A conclusion drawn from observations and reasoning rather than something recorded directly.
Systematic distortion arising from how an exposure, outcome, covariate, or other study variable is measured, classified, recalled, recorded, or collected.

A protein embedded in the bilayer itself and not removable by gentle extraction that leaves the bilayer intact. Most cross it, and those are transmembrane proteins; some sit in one leaflet only, so transmembrane is the narrower word rather than a synonym. Integral proteins diffuse laterally and rotate about an axis across the membrane, and they do not flip-flop, so the side each part of the protein faces is fixed for its working life.

A transmembrane receptor, made of an alpha and a beta subunit, by which a cell binds the matrix outside it. In the human intestinal crypt integrins bind the laminins and fibronectin of the basement membrane, and integrin-linked kinase provides a physical link from the integrin beta1 tail to actin. So the attachment facing downward is an actin-linked one, like two of the three that face sideways.
A comparison that keeps units in their originally assigned groups regardless of whether they received or used the assigned intervention.
The degree to which independent raters give the same ratings or classifications to the same cases under a stated coding rule and conditions.

The fitted value of the response when every predictor is zero, in the units of the response. It positions the line vertically and is often a statement about conditions nobody observed, as in this lesson where no one had a dinner-to-sleep interval of zero.

A rope-like cytoskeletal polymer, apolar because its dimers associate in an anti-parallel fashion into tetramers with no net direction. It is the floppiest of the three systems as a single filament, with a persistence length of a few hundred nanometres to about a micrometre, and the toughest under stretch, extending beyond 200 per cent of its resting length without breaking and stiffening as it is strained further. Because it is apolar it carries no molecular motors, so nothing travels along one in a chosen direction. That is a statement about transport and not about passivity: intermediate filament networks are regulated, are remodelled, and take part in signalling, adhesion dynamics and cell mechanics through cross-talk with the other two systems.
The degree to which a study's own comparison supports the conclusion drawn about the people or items that were in it.

The part of the cell cycle outside M phase, comprising G1, S phase and G2. A cell in interphase is not resting: it grows, makes protein, and in S phase replicates its DNA. In an illustrative cultured human cycle of about 24 hours, interphase occupies roughly 95 per cent of the time, which is why a snapshot of any tissue shows very few cells caught in the act of dividing.
Using a fitted relationship at a predictor value inside the range the data covered, where observations exist on both sides of the value being asked about.

The upper quartile minus the lower quartile, that is the width of the middle half of an ordered data set, in the unit of the data. It describes variability near the centre and is usually less sensitive to outliers than the range.
A numerical scale on which differences are meaningful but the zero point is arbitrary, so ratios of displayed values depend on the chosen origin.

A numerical scale on which differences between values are meaningful while the zero point is a convention, so ratios of the displayed values depend on the chosen origin. Temperature in degrees Celsius is the standard case.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning PREM-QNT-003 already gives the term: differences are meaningful, the zero point is arbitrary, and ratios of displayed values therefore depend on the origin. This lesson adds only the consequence for summaries, that an interval scale supports a mean and a standard deviation while it does not support a ratio between two values.

uses.definition: Evidence from a design in which an investigator deliberately assigns or changes an exposure, treatment, process, or condition and compares outcomes.
A calculated quantity that remains constant under an exact model, such as y/x for direct proportion or xy for inverse proportion.
In this lesson's nondegenerate family comparison, a relationship y = k/x with fixed nonzero k, in which the product xy equals k wherever x is nonzero.
A function such as arcsin, arccos, or arctan that returns a principal angle from a trigonometric ratio.

The set of attachment structures joining one epithelial cell to its neighbours, arranged in a fixed order from the apical surface downward: tight junction, then adherens junction, then desmosomes. The word complex invites the assumption that they work as one machine, and this lesson's evidence is that they do not: each grips its own cytoskeletal polymer and each fails separately.

The intermediate filament protein family of epithelial cells, and so the polymer an epithelial desmosome anchors. In this lesson keratin is the tension-bearing member of the cytoskeleton: it is what desmoplakin grips, and its mechanical properties are the intermediate filament properties described above.

The protein structure assembled on a centromere, to which spindle microtubules attach and which reports its own attachment state to the spindle assembly checkpoint. Each of the two sister chromatids carries one. A kinetochore that is not properly engaged assembles the complex that blocks anaphase, and a single such kinetochore is enough to hold an entire cell. Exactly which physical variable a kinetochore reports, whether microtubule occupancy or mechanical tension, is unresolved.

A chromatid left behind near the spindle midzone during anaphase instead of travelling cleanly to a pole, characteristically the consequence of a merotelic attachment pulling it in two directions. A laggard that persists there to the end of division is packaged into a micronucleus. Note that lagging and missegregating are different events: a laggard can end up in the correct daughter cell.

Movement of a lipid or protein within the plane of one leaflet, past its neighbours. It is fast: a lipid swaps places with a neighbour about ten million times a second, giving a diffusion coefficient near one square micrometre per second, so a lipid crosses a cell-sized distance in a couple of minutes.

The result that the observed relative frequency of an event across independent repeated trials converges to its probability as the number of trials grows. It constrains the share over a long record and says nothing about the next trial, so it never implies that a short-run deviation will be repaid.

One of the two layers of lipid making up a bilayer. In a plasma membrane the outer or exoplasmic leaflet faces the space outside the cell and the inner or cytoplasmic leaflet faces the cytoplasm. The two hold different lipids, and this lesson treats that difference as one of the two main organising facts about membranes.

The single straight line for which the sum of the squared vertical distances from the observed points is as small as it can be. Distances are measured in the response because the line is used to describe the response, and they are squared so that misses in opposite directions cannot cancel.

The property of a column that decides which arithmetic its values will support, fixed by how the values were produced rather than by how they are stored. The four levels used here are nominal, ordinal, interval, and ratio.

A property determined by how extreme an observation's predictor values are relative to the rest of the design; in a one-predictor fit, points near the ends of the predictor range have higher leverage. Leverage is distinct from a large residual: an observation is especially influential when high leverage is combined with a residual large enough to move the fitted line. The everyday sense of leverage, meaning advantage gained over something, is unrelated.
