An extracellular signal molecule considered in its capacity as the thing that binds a receptor. Signal and ligand can pick out the same molecule; the word ligand puts the emphasis on the binding event rather than on the sending.

A receptor in which the ligand-binding site and an ion channel belong to one protein, so that binding opens the channel directly and ions flow. Nothing has to be synthesised and no separate messenger has to be found; what crosses the membrane is charge. Receptors of this kind are also called ionotropic, in contrast with metabotropic receptors that work through second messengers, though in the insect chemosensory literature Ionotropic Receptor also names one particular gene family, which is a narrower use of the word and not a synonym for this entry.

A display that joins points measured in sequence, usually over time, so that the space between two points stands for the interval the quantity travelled through. It encodes a value by position rather than by length, so its vertical axis may be restricted to a stated range.
The multiplier applied to corresponding lengths; areas and volumes scale by its square and cube respectively.

Two facing layers of lipid molecules with their water-avoiding tails buried between them and their water-attracting heads exposed to water on each side. It is the structural core of every biological membrane and is about 5 nanometres thick overall, with a water-avoiding interior of about 3 to 3.5 nanometres.

A patch of membrane in which glycolipids, sphingomyelin and cholesterol pack more tightly and move less freely than the surrounding bilayer, while still remaining fluid. Such domains form in the outer leaflet and are unusually large and stable in the enterocyte brush border. The model of these domains remains under active discussion in the field.
A table or graph using logarithms of both positive variables, in which a power law becomes linear.
The exponent to which a valid base must be raised to produce a positive argument.

The open space inside a tube or hollow organ, and the side of an epithelium that faces it. In the colon the lumen holds the gut contents, including the bacterial population the epithelium keeps out of the tissue.

A compartment held near pH 5 by a proton pump in its membrane, containing acid hydrolases that break down material taken into the cell and worn-out organelles. The acid interior is not a convenience for the enzymes. It is what switches them on, and therefore also what makes them safe for the cell to own.

The factor by which an instrument enlarges the apparent size of an object. Magnification and spatial resolution are separate quantities: enlarging an image past an instrument's resolution limit produces a larger blur without revealing finer spatial detail. Magnification alone also does not determine detection or localisation, which depend on contrast, labelling, sampling and noise.
The nonnegative length or Euclidean norm of a vector.

Half the width of a confidence interval: the multiplier times the standard error, in the units of the estimate. It is the distance you reach out from the estimate in each direction, and doubling it gives the interval's width.
Keeping a specified person or role unaware of specified study information, such as group assignment, to block that knowledge from influencing conduct or assessment.

alignment.note: Adopts PREM-SCI-005's term-blinding meaning. This lesson displays masking as the primary label and retains blinding as the same course concept.

uses.definition: The arithmetic mean: the sum of the values divided by how many there are. Computing it uses the distances between values, so it reports something about the cases only when those distances are fixed and knowable.
Closeness of agreement between a measured value and the value of the quantity being measured; accuracy is a qualitative concept and is not the same as precision.
The difference between a measured value and an appropriate reference quantity value; it can be described as having random and systematic components in a stated measurement model.
How closely replicate measured values agree when obtained under specified conditions; precision describes dispersion and does not by itself establish closeness to a reference.
Evidence about the existence or details of the entities, activities, ordered changes, and conditions that connect a proposed cause to an outcome.
Evidence that bears on the entities, interactions, sequence, and constraints proposed to produce an outcome.

The middle position once values are placed in order. With an even number of ordinal categories, the two middle observations define a middle pair or interval unless they fall in the same category; averaging their numerical codes would assume spacing the categories do not establish. For measured amounts, the usual numerical median is the average of the two middle values when there is an even number.

The middle value once the observations are placed in order, or the average of the two middle values when the count is even. It answers which value splits the group in half. Because it is determined by ranks rather than by magnitudes, changing how extreme an extreme value is does not move it.

An intermediate factor through which the independent variable produces some or all of its effect on the dependent variable; unlike a confounder, it is part of the proposed causal pathway rather than a separate rival explanation.
A variable on a proposed causal route from exposure to outcome that carries some part of the effect under the stated model.

alignment.note: Same concept as Lesson 3 (an intermediate factor carrying part of the effect), restated on the exposure-to-outcome causal route used in this lesson.

uses.definition: The division that produces gametes: one round of DNA replication followed by two cell divisions, so that a diploid cell gives rise to haploid products. Its first division separates the members of each homologous pair from each other and its second separates sister chromatids, and it happens only in the germ line. A somatic tissue such as the colonic crypt never performs it.

The process in which meiosis deliberately breaks its own DNA and repairs each break using the homolog as the template. Most breaks are repaired without any exchange of arms; where the repair does produce a reciprocal exchange, the outcome is crossing over. Where this lesson writes recombination without qualification it means this meiotic process; the bare word is broader in general use and covers other kinds of DNA exchange that this lesson does not treat.

The maintained difference in composition between the two leaflets of a membrane. In a eukaryotic plasma membrane, phosphatidylcholine and the sphingolipids sit mainly outside while phosphatidylserine, phosphatidylethanolamine and the phosphoinositides are held inside. Slow flip-flop lets the difference persist; ATP-driven transporters create it.

A qualitative summary of how easily the hydrocarbon chains in a bilayer move and how loosely they pack. The measurable quantities behind the word are viscosity and chain order; this lesson uses it as a direction of travel rather than as a number, which is what the outcome asks a learner to predict.

The difference in electrical potential between the inside of a cell and the fluid outside it, conventionally quoted as inside minus outside and normally negative in an animal cell. It supplies the electrical half of the electrochemical gradient. The sodium-potassium ATPase contributes to it by removing one net positive charge per cycle, though it is not the only contributor.

The movement of a solute from one side of a membrane to the other. The everyday sense of transport, goods carried somewhere in a vehicle that travels, survives only in the part about getting from one place to another: what moves a solute here is a protein fixed in the membrane, which goes nowhere itself. This is a different process from the vesicular transport of PREM-BIO-003, where a membrane-bounded container really does travel between compartments.

A sheet exactly two lipid molecules thick that separates one space from another, behaves as a liquid within its own plane, and controls what crosses it. The everyday sense of a thin separating sheet, as in a drum skin or the film inside an eggshell, keeps only the separating part. The plasma membrane is the one enclosing the whole cell.

A configuration in which a single kinetochore is connected to microtubules from both spindle poles at once. It does not trigger a checkpoint-dependent delay of anaphase, because like a correct attachment it generates tension across the sister kinetochores and leaves no kinetochore unattached. The chromatid is then pulled toward both poles and lags at anaphase. Merotely is the clean demonstration that a wrong state can satisfy a working checkpoint; it is not established as the main cause of aneuploidy, and that question is disputed.
A property of a measurement result that relates it to a stated reference through a documented, unbroken calibration chain in which each link contributes to measurement uncertainty.
The study of microscopic organisms and related biological entities, including how they grow, change, and interact with hosts and environments.

A millionth of a metre, and a thousandth of a millimetre, written µm. It is the working unit of cell biology: cells are measured in tens of micrometres and tissue structures in hundreds. Spatial detail finer than about a quarter of a micrometre is not resolved by a conventional light microscope, although a sufficiently contrasting or labelled sub-resolution feature may still be detected or localised.

A small separate nucleus formed around a chromatid that was left near the spindle midzone at the end of division, rather than being included in either daughter's main nucleus. It is the visible record that a division went mechanically wrong. What becomes of a cell carrying one is the subject of PREM-BIO-010 of this block, not of this lesson.

A hollow, polar polymer of tubulin about 25 nanometres in outside diameter, and by a wide margin the stiffest of the three filament systems: its persistence length exceeds a millimetre, which is more than forty times the height of an absorptive intestinal cell, so one microtubule crossing such a cell is effectively a straight rod. Kinesins and dyneins move along it, which makes it suited to defining an axis and running directed traffic along that axis.

One finger-like projection of an absorptive cell's apical surface, about a micrometre long and about a hundred nanometres across, held out against the surface tension of a fluid membrane by a core bundle of roughly 19 cross-linked actin filaments and guyed to that membrane by myosin cross-bridges. The plural is microvilli. A microvillus is a single projection and is not the array: the array is the brush border, and the two words are not interchangeable.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-004 glosses microvillus inside its brush border entry, as one projection of the array, and states that the two words are not interchangeable. This lesson keeps that distinction exactly and promotes the single projection to its own term, because the projection's actin core is this lesson's subject. The array sense stays with the earlier lesson's brush border entry; microvillus is not an alias of it. Readers should note that PREM-BIO-003 and PREM-BIO-004 give brush border slightly different definitions, and this lesson follows PREM-BIO-004's figures.

uses.definition: The smallest change in an outcome measure that patients perceive as beneficial. It belongs to a specified outcome and population and to a patient-referenced judgement of meaningful change. Sample data can contribute through anchor-based or distribution-based estimation, but variation within the sample cannot by itself establish what patients perceive as beneficial, and a value lifted from a different population needs a clinical argument before reuse.

An allocation method that uses selected baseline factors to favour the assignment that reduces current imbalance. It may be deterministic or include a random component, so the method must be described rather than assumed to be random from its name.
Assignment of a unit to an incorrect category for an exposure, outcome, or other variable.

A compartment whose boundary is part of its mechanism. The electron transport chain pumps protons across that boundary and the return flow of protons drives ATP synthase. Because a gradient is a difference between two sides, removing the boundary removes the device instead of merely opening it.

The sorting of duplicated chromosomes into two complete sets, conventionally divided into prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. Each transition is better read as a condition than as a scene change: condensed chromosomes appear, microtubules attach to kinetochores, and anaphase begins when the link between sister chromatids is broken. Mitosis is the sorting; cutting the cell in two is cytokinesis, a separate operation with its own machinery and its own checkpoint.

The tetrameric complex of MAD2, CDC20, BUBR1 and BUB3 that assembles in response to kinetochores that are not correctly attached, and that binds APC/C-CDC20 to block its activity. It is the physical form the spindle assembly checkpoint's signal takes, and it is what a single unattached kinetochore is enough to keep supplied.

The escape of a cell from a spindle-checkpoint arrest without having divided, leaving one cell containing both sets of chromosomes. It happens because cyclin B is slowly destroyed throughout the arrest even while the checkpoint remains demonstrably active, until too little remains to sustain the mitotic state. In human retinal pigment epithelial cells the arrest lasted on the order of nine to fifteen hours before slippage. This is why a checkpoint should be understood as a delay with a limit rather than as a gate.

The microtubule apparatus built at mitosis that attaches to kinetochores and pulls the sister chromatids to opposite poles. It does a second job that is easy to miss: the position of the anaphase spindle also determines where the cleavage furrow forms, so the structure that sorts the chromosomes is the structure that locates the cut. A cell therefore never has to work out where its own middle is.
The value or category that occurs most often in a set of recorded values. It needs no order and no scale, so it is available at every level of measurement.

For a sample, the exact value that occurs most often. It is informative for data recorded as a small number of fixed levels or categories. In finely measured continuous samples, exact repeats depend on measurement precision, so a modal histogram interval or a population-density mode can be more informative. A distribution can have more than one mode.
A condition or simplification accepted so the model can represent selected relationships, such as treating a process as constant, negligible, or well mixed.
The purposes, conditions, scales, and contexts for which a model has a defensible basis of use.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-007 uses domain for the set of allowable inputs to a function. Here model domain is broader: the supported purposes, conditions, scales, and contexts for applying a scientific model.

uses.definition: A value, condition, or record supplied to a model for a particular use or run.
The prediction, estimate, explanation, classification, or other result produced by applying a model.
A model quantity treated as fixed during one run but available to change between runs, systems, or calibration choices.
A quantity represented in the model whose value can differ among states, observations, or times.

alignment.note: Narrows the established general sense of a variable to a quantity explicitly represented in a model whose value can differ among states, observations, or times.

uses.definition: Evidence about molecular identity, structure, interaction, reaction, or change that can test one or more links in a proposed mechanism.

A substance that spreads from a source and specifies what cells become according to its local concentration. Wnt in the colonic crypt fits the second half of that description comfortably: what a cell becomes does depend on how much reaches it. Whether it fits the first half in the classical sense of diffusive spreading is an open question, because Wnt proteins are lipid-modified and their mode of travel is debated. This lesson uses the word for the role Wnt plays and not as a claim about how it moves.

A protein that spends chemical energy to move along a polar cytoskeletal filament in a particular direction, carrying a load or generating force. Myosins move on actin filaments; kinesins and dyneins move on microtubules. A motor requires a filament whose ends differ, which is why intermediate filaments have none.

A regression with more than one predictor, each carrying its own coefficient. Each coefficient reports the fitted change in the response per unit of its own predictor while the other predictors stay where they are, which is what a report means when it calls a result adjusted for those variables.

The rule for the probability that two events both occur: multiply the probability of one by the conditional probability of the other given it. When the events are independent the conditional factor equals the unconditional probability and the rule reduces to the plain product of the two probabilities.

The situation in which a study carries out more than one hypothesis test, so that each additional test is another opportunity for a Type I error and the study's overall chance of at least one false alarm exceeds the level any single test was set at.
A systematic analysis across many reasonable data-processing or analytic paths to reveal which choices materially affect a result.

Two events that cannot both occur on the same trial, so the probability that both occur is zero and the probability that at least one occurs is the plain sum of their probabilities. Being in the early-dinner group and being in the late-dinner group is such a pair.

A study of exposure variation created by an external event, policy, rule, or implementation process rather than assigned by the research team; the assignment process must be examined before making experiment-like claims.
A study of exposure variation created by an external rule, event, policy, or allocation process whose assignment must be examined before experiment-like causal claims are made.

alignment.note: Adopts Lesson 4's meaning: exposure variation created by an external process rather than by the researcher.

uses.definition: The logarithm with base e, written ln.

A description of how a dead cell looks: swollen, with its plasma membrane given way and its contents released into the surrounding tissue, usually with inflammation present. The word names an appearance and not a cause. A necrotic-looking death may have been accidental or may have run through a dedicated pathway such as necroptosis or pyroptosis, and a tissue section alone does not distinguish those.
A control condition expected to show the baseline or no tested response, used to reveal background signal or a response where none is expected.
An exposure or outcome chosen to lack the tested causal relation while sharing important bias-producing conditions, so an unexpected association can signal systematic error.

alignment.note: Lesson 3 defines a negative control as a physical baseline condition in an experiment, expected to show no response. Here it is a causal-inference probe: a chosen exposure or outcome that should lack the tested relation but share the biases. Same logic (an effect here means something is off), different object.

uses.definition: Among people whose test was negative, the share who do not have the target condition: P(condition absent given test negative). It divides the true negatives by a group defined by the test result, and it rises as the condition becomes less common in the group tested, moving opposite to the positive predictive value.

The stochastic replacement of stem cells in which no lineage has an advantage, so that a lineage's descendants expand or vanish by chance, following a one-dimensional random walk. In human colonic crypts it means that all but one stem lineage eventually disappears and the crypt becomes the descendant of a single stem cell, with a median time of about 6.3 years. It is why a mutation in one crypt stem cell has a chance of taking over the crypt without needing to confer any benefit.

The number an effect would take if the two groups being compared were the same: zero for a difference between two averages. Checking whether an interval contains it is the first thing most readers do, and it answers only whether the direction is supported.
A categorical variable whose groups carry no inherent order, so the list of groups can be rearranged without losing information. Sex, blood group, and admitting ward are examples.

The failure of chromosomes to separate normally during a division, leaving one product with an extra copy and another with none. In meiosis it can happen at either division, and the two cases leave different signatures: a failure at the first division yields products carrying two different homologs, and a failure at the second yields a product carrying two copies of one homolog.

One specific continuous probability distribution: symmetric about its centre, single-humped, and fixed entirely by a mean and a standard deviation. The name collides with two other senses a reader already holds. In plain English normal means usual; in a clinic a normal result is one inside a laboratory reference range. Neither is implied here, and a measurement can follow a normal distribution while every value in it is clinically alarming.

A member of a superfamily of intracellular transcription factors activated by lipophilic ligands. These receptors do not sit in the plasma membrane, and their ligands cross it unaided, so no binding event on the outside has to be converted into one on the inside. What sets them apart from other receptors is that they mediate transcription without intermediate signalling cascades, binding their target genes directly. A nuclear receptor is one kind of intracellular receptor; the broader term also covers intracellular receptors that are not transcription factors, so the two are not interchangeable.
The region of a prokaryotic cell where the DNA is concentrated. It is not separated from the rest of the cytoplasm by a membrane, which is the single feature that distinguishes it from a nucleus.

The distribution of results the null model predicts across repeats of the study. For the dinner-timing difference this lesson uses a normal approximation centred on 0 mg/dL with an estimated standard error of 4.13 mg/dL. A p-value is an area measured on the selected distribution, which is why the shape of the curve is itself a modelling assumption.

A statement fixing the quantity under study at one specified value, adopted so that a model can predict what data should look like if it held. In this lesson it sets the true difference in mean fasting glucose between the late and early dinner groups at 0 mg/dL. It is adopted as a starting assumption for calculation and carries no suggestion that anyone believes it.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-002 defines a hypothesis as a proposed explanation or relationship from which observable expectations can be derived. A null hypothesis is one of those, narrowed in two ways: it must fix a numerical quantity at a single stated value, and it is adopted for the purpose of being tested against rather than because it is the explanation on offer. The scientific hypothesis in the dinner-timing study is that later dinners raise fasting glucose; the null hypothesis is its numerical foil, and scene 2 bridges the two senses where the word first appears in the new sense.

uses.definition: The reciprocal of a beneficial absolute risk reduction for a specified outcome and comparison: the number of people who would have to receive one condition instead of the other, over a stated period, for one additional person to benefit. A non-integer patient count is conventionally rounded upward. A zero reduction has no finite number needed to treat; if the intervention increases an unwanted outcome, the corresponding reciprocal is a number needed to harm. The measure is incomplete without its time period, comparison, and baseline risk.
The number multiplying a unit when a quantity is expressed in that unit.
A record of what was noticed or measured, stated so that its object, conditions, and result can be checked.
A study in which researchers do not assign the exposure being compared but record exposure and outcome differences that occur.
An information-bias mechanism in which an assessor's knowledge or predisposition influences a judgment, measurement, classification, or recording decision.

alignment.note: Relates this observer-knowledge mechanism to PREM-SCI-005's term-detection-bias. Detection bias can include broader systematic differences in outcome assessment, so it is not treated here as an exact alias.

uses.definition: The odds in one group divided by the odds in the other, equal to the cross-product of the diagonals of a two-by-two table of counts. It approximates the risk ratio when the outcome is rare and sits further from 1 than the risk ratio when the outcome is common, so it may not be read as a risk ratio without checking how often the outcome occurred.

The probability that an event occurs divided by the probability that it does not, which counting people is cases per non-case. Odds and risk carry the same information and convert freely, by odds = risk / (1 - risk) and risk = odds / (1 + odds). The betting sense of the word contributes only the cases-to-non-cases form, and nothing about stakes or payouts.

A gene whose activation contributes to the growth advantage of a cell. In this lesson oncogenes appear twice and in opposite directions: introducing v-Ha-ras or v-src into epithelial cells abolished their attachment-dependent death, while activating an oncogene can also drive a cell into permanent arrest. Which of those a cell does is not decided by the oncogene alone.

The permanent proliferative arrest a cell may enter in response to activation of an oncogene. The change that ought to make the cell divide without limit instead stops it dividing at all, which is why senescence is read as a response that suppresses cancer rather than as a failure of the cell.

Oogenesis is the production of egg cells in the ovary; spermatogenesis is the production of sperm cells in the testis. Both run meiosis and they run it differently: spermatogenesis divides symmetrically to four functional gametes and continues throughout life, while oogenesis divides asymmetrically to one functional gamete, begins before birth, and arrests in the first division for decades.
Procedural and analytic information made sufficiently inspectable for another person to understand and, where feasible and permitted, re-run or repeat the work.
A specified procedure or rule that turns a target quantity or construct into an observable record.

Treatment of dehydration from diarrhoeal illness by giving a solution of salt and glucose by mouth, so that sodium is absorbed through the intact glucose-coupled cotransport route and water follows osmotically. It replaces what is being lost: the standard glucose-based solution does not stop the secretion, shorten the illness, or clear the infection. The therapy is the practice and the solution is the substance it uses, so the two are not interchangeable words. Discussed in this lesson strictly as the setting for a transport mechanism, with no composition, dose, or regimen stated anywhere.

A power-of-ten description of a quantity's approximate scale. Two quantities are of the same order when their ratio is nearer to 1 than to 10. This lesson compares sizes and counts by order of magnitude first and only then looks at the digits, because every quantity it uses is an estimate for a reference body or a representative case.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning PREM-QNT-005 already gives the term, a power-of-ten description of a quantity's approximate scale, and does not restate the arithmetic. This lesson is where that arithmetic earns its keep: every size, threshold, and count in cell biology is a band rather than a constant, and comparing bands by their power of ten is how the block reasons throughout.

uses.definition: A power-of-ten description of a number's rough scale, used here as a coarse prediction rather than an exact value.
A power-of-ten description of a quantity's approximate scale.

A categorical variable whose groups are ranked, so the order is part of what was recorded, while the size of the step between adjacent groups is not established. A four-point adherence rating, a triage level, and a tumour stage are examples.

A compartment, or in a few cases a structure, with a recognisable identity and a job the others do not do, holding its own distinct set of proteins. Naming an organelle is the end of an explanation and not the beginning of one; the question that does the work is which maintained condition it holds.
Evidence about a response or phenotype in an intact organism, where many tissues, processes, behaviours, and environmental inputs can interact.

The movement of water across a membrane in response to a difference in effective osmolality, from the side where water is less constrained by solute towards the side where it is more so. Water is moved this way and is not pumped: no protein drives water against its own gradient, so the only way a cell shifts water is by shifting solute and letting water follow.

A compound that inhibits the sodium-potassium ATPase specifically. It is used in this lesson as an experimental tool: because it acts on the pump in the basolateral membrane and not on the apical cotransporter, the fact that it stops brush-border glucose transport shows that the effect travels through the sodium gradient rather than through any contact with the transporter itself.
The person or process that measures, scores, or adjudicates the study outcome. Blinding this role is the usual protection when participants themselves cannot be blinded.
The response, event, state, or measurement that a study records and compares.
The response, event, state, or measurement a study compares across exposure or assignment conditions.

alignment.note: Adopts Lesson 4's meaning: the response a study records and compares across conditions.

uses.definition: An observation lying far enough from the rest of the data to stand apart from them in a display. A histogram or scatter plot can flag one; whether it reflects the measurement, the record, or the person is a separate question the display cannot answer.

An observation that sits far from the bulk of the data. The label describes a position in the distribution and nothing more; an outlier may be a recording error, or it may be an accurate measurement of a person whose situation genuinely differs from the rest, and deciding which is a matter for the investigator rather than for the arithmetic.

The probability, computed on the assumption that the null hypothesis and every other assumption in the statistical model are correct, that the test statistic would be at least as extreme as the value actually observed. For the dinner-timing study the two-sided normal-approximation value is 0.029. It is a statement about data made under an assumption about the world, and it reports neither the probability that the null is true, nor the probability that chance produced the result, nor the size of any effect.

A protein that senses cellular stress, including DNA damage and excessive proliferative signalling, and can produce transient cell-cycle arrest, permanent arrest as senescence, or apoptosis. It therefore sits at the junction of all three routes this lesson describes. The gene encoding it is written TP53, and the two names are not interchangeable: TP53 is the gene and p53 the protein. TP53 is inactivated in more than half of all sporadic human cancers, and which of p53's three responses does the tumour-suppressing work is not a settled question and depends on the tissue.
Two sets of values matched one to one because repeated measurements came from the same case, so the file could be written with one row per pair.

Movement or permeability through the space between neighbouring epithelial cells, regulated by the junctions that join those cells. It depends on cell-to-cell organisation and differs from a transcellular route through one cell.

A fixed numerical property of the whole population, such as its mean or its standard deviation. A parameter is one definite number that nobody has measured; a statistic computed from a sample is an estimate of it.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a model parameter as a model quantity held fixed during one run and free to change between runs or calibrations. That is a setting the modeller chooses. The statistical sense used here is the opposite in one respect: a population parameter is a fact about the world that is fixed whether anyone knows it or not, and the whole point of a sample is to estimate it. Both senses are standard and the surrounding context decides which is meant; this lesson always means the population quantity.

uses.definition: A fixed unknown quantity belonging to the population a sample was drawn from, such as the true difference in average fasting glucose between two ways of eating. It has one value, that value does not change when you sample, and no study observes it directly.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a model parameter as a quantity an author sets or adjusts inside a scientific model to make it behave. The statistical sense used here is the opposite arrangement: nobody sets it and nobody can read it off, because it belongs to the population and the study exists to estimate it. Both senses are standard and the concept scene bridges them where the word first appears in this lesson.

uses.definition: A mutation present in a tumour that confers no selective growth advantage, carried along by the clone rather than contributing to it. More than 99.9 per cent of the alterations found in tumours are immaterial to the disease, which is why finding a mutation in a tumour is not evidence that the mutation did anything.
For an ordinary positive ratio-scale baseline, the change divided by the starting value, expressed as a percentage and labelled as an increase or decrease.
The arithmetic difference between two percentages, distinct from their relative percent change.
A ratio expressed per hundred relative to a named whole or reference quantity.

Distortion arising when participants or those delivering an intervention behave differently because they know the assigned condition — for example through changed effort, adherence, treatment sought elsewhere, or withdrawal.

A protein attached to one face of a membrane through interactions with other proteins rather than embedded in the bilayer, and releasable by gentle treatments such as extreme pH or high or low salt that leave the bilayer intact.

A compartment that runs oxidation reactions, including the breakdown of fatty acids too long for mitochondria to start on, and that carries catalase alongside the oxidases producing hydrogen peroxide, so the peroxide is destroyed where it is made. It segregates a reactive product, which is a different problem from the one the lysosome solves.

The distance along a filament over which it stays roughly straight against the random thermal motion of the surrounding water. Below that distance the filament behaves as a rod; well above it, the filament bends appreciably. It is the single number this lesson uses to compare filament stiffness, and it is only informative once divided by the length of the structure that has to be held.

The change of a bilayer between a liquid state, with chains bending and lipids sliding past one another, and a rigid crystalline state with the chains packed straight and parallel. The temperature at which it happens falls when chains are shorter or carry cis double bonds, and cholesterol obstructs the transition.
The study of how living structures function and regulate their internal conditions across cells, tissues, organs, and systems.
The evidence line or result that carries the greatest justified influence on the integrated conclusion for the specified question.

A small DNA loop separate from a bacterium's main chromosome, which the cell can gain, lose, or pass to a neighbour. Plasmid transfer is one route by which antibiotic resistance spreads between bacteria.
A test of whether a result is consistent with an estimate, bound, inverse operation, or contextual constraint; it can expose errors but does not prove correctness.

The single value a sample gives for a quantity you want to know, such as the 9.0 mg/dL difference this study measured. It is the best guess the sample supports and it carries no information about how far off it might be.

The small cell discarded at each of the two asymmetric divisions of oogenesis. Half the genome is segregated into the polar bodies, which is why one meiosis in the female yields a single functional gamete instead of four. The source this lesson follows describes two polar bodies, one per division; accounts giving three exist and the lesson records that disagreement rather than settling it.
Evidence about patterns, variation, associations, or effects across a defined group of people or other organisms, settings, or times.
The study of health patterns and their distribution across groups, together with the biological, behavioural, social, and environmental conditions related to those patterns.

The complete group a study means to describe, as opposed to the sample it actually measured. In this lesson the population has numerical properties of its own, including a mean and a standard deviation, and the sample's job is to estimate them.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-005 defines the target population as the whole group a study is meant to describe, as distinct from the group it enrolled, and this lesson keeps that meaning unchanged. What it adds is that the population has a mean and a standard deviation of its own, which are the quantities a sample mean and sample standard deviation estimate. The earlier lesson's point still governs everything here: a sample can at best speak for the frame it was drawn from, and no standard error repairs a frame that missed the intended population.

uses.definition: What a cell can determine about where it sits from a quantity it can measure locally. Treating it as information is what makes it countable: telling apart 32 positions demands five binary distinctions, and a single gene reading a single threshold on a gradient that falls in one direction supplies one, distinguishing two regions and no more. A gradient therefore supplies coarse zones rather than coordinates, and real systems exceed that ceiling by letting genes influence one another and by using graded expression rather than on-or-off calls.
A control condition expected to produce a known response, used to check that the system can reveal the signal of interest.

Among people whose test was positive, the share who have the target condition: P(condition present given test positive). It divides the true positives by a group defined by the test result, so it describes the person holding that result, and it falls as the condition becomes less common in the group tested. Note that a positive result means the test fired, which for most tests is unwelcome news.
In this lesson's family comparison, a relationship y = kx^p with fixed nonzero constant k and exponent p over a stated domain.

The probability that a test rejects the null hypothesis when a stated alternative is true: power equals one minus beta. It rises with the size of the true effect and the sample size, and falls with the variability of the measurement and with a stricter significance level. A power figure quoted without naming the effect it was computed against describes nothing.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-010 uses power in the algebraic sense, in the relationship y = kx^p where p is the exponent of a power law, and PREM-QNT-001 defines an exponent in the same family of meanings. Statistical power shares nothing with that sense beyond the word: it is a probability between 0 and 1 attached to a study design, and no exponent is involved. The orientation scene names the collision with both the algebraic sense and the everyday sense of force or authority before the term is used.

uses.definition: The property of an effect that is large enough to change a decision someone is actually facing. Judging it requires the effect estimate in the units of the decision, a threshold saying how much would be enough, and a view of what acting would cost. Only the first of those comes out of a statistical analysis, so this judgement is made by people and not returned by a test.

How closely repeated attempts at the same quantity agree with one another. Applied to an estimate, it means how tightly the distribution of repeated estimates clusters around its population target, which is what the standard error measures. Precision says nothing about whether the estimate is aimed at the right population.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-006 defines measurement precision as how closely replicate measured values agree under specified conditions, and warns that precision describes dispersion without establishing closeness to a reference. This lesson keeps that meaning and extends what is being replicated: instead of repeating a measurement on one thing, the repeat is the whole study on a fresh sample. The earlier lesson's warning carries across intact, and the clinical wrap-up restates it as the point that a larger sample buys precision and nothing else.

uses.definition: How tightly a study has pinned down the quantity it set out to estimate, read directly from the width of its interval. A narrow interval is a precise result and a wide one is an imprecise result, whatever the estimate at the centre happens to be.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-006 owns measurement precision, which is how closely repeated measurements of the same thing by the same instrument agree. The sense used here is a property of a whole study's estimate, and the two are related without being the same: a precise instrument reduces the spread that feeds the standard error, but sample size moves this kind of precision and instrument quality alone cannot. The width scene keeps the two apart where they meet.

uses.definition: An observable result expected if a stated hypothesis holds under stated conditions.
A dated research plan recorded before the relevant outcomes are known so planned decisions can be distinguished from later changes and exploration.

A comparison named in the study protocol before the data were seen. Prespecification separates planned tests from data-selected ones and improves interpretability, but it does not remove multiplicity when several comparisons were planned; a confirmatory strategy must also allocate its error rate across the planned family.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-009 defines preregistration as a dated research plan recorded before the relevant outcomes are known, so that planned decisions can be told apart from later changes and exploration. This lesson keeps that meaning and adds the multiplicity boundary: prespecification prevents data-driven selection but does not remove the need to control the family-wise error rate when several confirmatory comparisons are planned. The earlier lesson's distinction between planned and exploratory analysis is used here without being redefined.

uses.definition: The proportion of a defined population with a specified condition or characteristic at a stated time or over a stated period.

The proportion of a defined population with a specified condition or characteristic at a stated time or over a stated period. In this lesson it is the share of a tested group whose reference standard says the target condition is present. The toy comparison changes this quantity while stipulating unchanged sensitivity and specificity so that its effect on predictive values can be isolated.

alignment.note: Adopts the definition established by PREM-SCI-004 without change: the proportion of a defined population with a specified condition at a stated time. This lesson applies that meaning to the group a test is used in, and shows that it is what separates a test's detection measures from its predictive values.

uses.definition: Active transport in which the protein moving the solute is itself the protein that consumes the energy source, which in animal cells means it hydrolyses ATP. The sodium-potassium ATPase is the example this lesson uses. A cell deprived of ATP loses primary active transport essentially at once, because the molecule being consumed has gone.
The designated nonnegative even root, or the unique real odd root, represented by a radical symbol.

The height of a continuous distribution's curve at a given value. Density is not probability: probability is area under the curve between two values, so the probability that a continuous measurement takes any one exact value is zero, and a question about a continuous measurement has to name a range before it has an answer.

A rule assigning a probability to every range of values a measurement could take, describing the population a reading is drawn from rather than the readings in hand. For a measurement that can take any value in a range it is drawn as a curve, and probability is read as the area under that curve between two values.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-002 uses distribution for the observed shape of a set of measured values, read off a histogram of the data you have. A probability distribution is the idealised object standing behind those values: it covers readings nobody recorded, extends past both ends of the data, and assigns probability rather than counts. The lesson draws the second over the first and then checks whether the fit holds.

uses.definition: A named probability distribution adopted to represent how one measurement is spread across its possible values, together with the parameter values chosen for it. Adopting one is a decision that can be checked against data and rejected, and this lesson treats the normal curve fitted to cohort fasting glucose as exactly that.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a scientific model broadly as a selective representation of a system built to answer a stated question. This lesson narrows the word to one job: representing the spread of a single measurement across its possible values. It keeps the earlier lesson's discipline of stated assumptions, a domain of use, and tests that can fail, and it drops any claim about mechanism.

uses.definition: Drawing a sample from the sampling frame by a chance mechanism that gives every member a known chance of selection; the simplest version is plain random selection. It supports generalizing from the sample toward the frame's population. Random selection decides who enters a study and is distinct from random allocation, which decides which arm an already-entered participant joins.

A number between 0 and 1 attached to a stated event under stated conditions. This lesson reads it as the relative frequency the event settles toward across many repetitions, which is what makes it checkable against a record.

In the usage recommended by the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death, the regulated forms of cell death that run in ordinary physiology, without any perturbation from outside the organism. Apoptosis is one of them and is the one this lesson develops, so the two words are not synonyms: programmed cell death is the category and apoptosis is a member of it.

A cell whose DNA is not enclosed by a membrane envelope of its own but lies in the cytoplasm, in a dense region called the nucleoid. Bacteria and archaea are prokaryotic. The term names one architectural feature and carries no implication about age, complexity, size, or division rate, despite an etymology meaning before the kernel. The word covers both bacteria and archaea, which are not each other's closest relatives, so it names a way of being built rather than one group of relatives. At least one bacterium keeps its chromosomes inside membrane-bound compartments and is a bacterium regardless, because ancestry decides that and architecture does not.

The part of a renewing tissue whose cells are currently dividing. In a human colonic crypt it occupies the bottom third of the tube and accounts for about a quarter of the crypt's cells, identified by staining for the proliferation antigen Ki-67. It contains a small number of stem cells and a much larger number of transit-amplifying cells, and its size relative to the whole crypt is the quantity from which this lesson derives the tissue's cycle time.

The share of a tissue's cells that are dividing, obtained by dividing the number of proliferating cells by the total. For the human colonic crypt counted by Ki-67 staining it is about 0.257. It is more useful than either count on its own, because published totals for a crypt disagree while the ratio is what determines the compartment's cycle time: multiply the proliferative fraction by the tissue's turnover time and the crypt's size cancels out.

An equation asserting that two ratios are equal, for example a/b = c/d. This differs from the statistical sense of proportion as a part-to-whole fraction between 0 and 1, introduced in later data-analysis lessons.

In this block, a part divided by the whole it belongs to, giving one number between 0 and 1 that reports a group's share. Thirty-six women among sixty participants is a proportion of 0.6, or 60 per cent.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-003 uses proportion for an equation stating that two ratios are equal, as in a/b = c/d. Statistics uses the same word for a single part-to-whole fraction between 0 and 1. Both come from division, and the statistical sense always divides a part by the total it belongs to. The second scene names the collision where the word first appears in its new sense.

uses.definition: A part divided by the whole it belongs to, so a value between 0 and 1. Thirteen of sixty people gives a proportion of 0.217, which the same fact reported as a percentage calls 21.7%.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-003 defines a proportion as an equation asserting that two ratios are equal, such as a/b = c/d, which a learner solves for an unknown. This block uses the statistical sense: a part-to-whole fraction between 0 and 1 attached to a count. Both senses are standard and neither replaces the other; the surrounding context decides which is meant, and the concept scene bridges them where the word first appears here.

uses.definition: A part measured against the whole it came from, expressed as a number between 0 and 1. Every probability computed by counting in this lesson is a proportion in this sense: the count of outcomes in the event over the count of outcomes in the group being counted inside.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-003 defines a proportion as an equation asserting that two ratios are equal, such as a/b = c/d, and flags that data-analysis lessons use the word differently. This lesson introduces that second, statistical sense: a part measured against its whole. Both senses are standard and neither replaces the other; the opening scene names the collision before the word is used, and only the part-to-whole sense appears afterwards.

uses.definition: A fitted quantitative relationship of the form y = kx^p with fixed nonzero k, including the direct (p = 1) and inverse (p = -1) cases, proposed for data, identified from an invariant, parameterized, and checked against observations and assumptions.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a scientific model broadly as a selective representation of a system built to answer a stated question. This lesson narrows 'model' to a specific fitted quantitative relationship y = kx^p, judged by fit, residuals, and assumptions rather than by mechanism — an economical summary of how a response scales, not a claim about why.

uses.definition: The fixed nonzero multiplier k relating variables in this lesson's nondegenerate proportional models.
A cohort assembled before the outcomes of interest occur and followed forward as new outcomes are recorded.

The machinery that gets each product to the compartment or the cell face where it works: a destination encoded in the product, and a receptor able to read it. The mannose 6-phosphate group added to lysosomal enzymes in the Golgi, and recognised by mannose 6-phosphate receptors in the trans-Golgi network, is one complete example. Targeting can fail on its own, leaving a correctly made product in the wrong place.

A difference in hydrogen-ion concentration between the two sides of a membrane, which is what the pH values in this lesson describe and what the arithmetic here computes. A membrane usually also carries a difference in charge, the membrane potential, and the two together make the proton-motive force, or proton electrochemical potential, which is the quantity that drives ATP synthase in the mitochondrion. The chemical and electrical parts are separable, and this lesson computes only the chemical one.
Distortion of the accessible evidence base when a whole study's chance of becoming available depends on the nature or strength of its results.
A variable whose values are amounts on a measurement scale, so the difference between two values is itself a quantity that can be stated.
A measurable or specified property whose value can be expressed as a numerical value multiplied by a unit.

One of the three values that cut an ordered data set into four parts of equal size. The lower quartile Q1 sits at the 25th percentile, the second quartile is the median, and the upper quartile Q3 sits at the 75th percentile. Software packages use slightly different interpolation rules, so reported quartiles can differ a little on the same small sample.

A reversible state in which a cell is not cycling but can be brought back into the cycle, commonly labelled G0. The evidence is that it is a separate biological state and not simply a long G1, and that it is not one state but a heterogeneous collection of related conditions; distinguishing a quiescent cell from a cell in early G1 is difficult in practice. Most crypt stem cells are not dividing at any given moment, which is consistent with PREM-BIO-001's point that a stem cell is defined by capacity rather than by continuous activity.
A plane-angle unit defined by arc length divided by radius; a full turn is 2 pi radians.

Using a prespecified procedure that defines possible assignments and their probabilities before allocation and selects among them through chance. The procedure may use baseline characteristics through stratification or another restriction while retaining a random component; in some restricted methods, an upcoming assignment can become guessable without making the original sequence non-random.
Allocation by a chance process that gives each eligible unit a known chance of receiving each study condition and makes groups comparable in expectation.
Allocation by a chance process with known assignment probabilities that makes pre-assignment causes comparable across groups in expectation.

alignment.note: Adopts Lesson 4's meaning: allocation by a chance process with known probabilities that makes groups comparable in expectation.

uses.definition: Unpredictable variation that changes across repetitions and contributes imprecision rather than a stable systematic shift; it includes sampling variation and unpredictable measurement variation.
The component of measurement error that varies unpredictably across replicate measurements under stated conditions and appears as dispersion among results.
Assignment by a chance process that gives each eligible unit a defined allocation possibility and tends to balance prognostic factors between comparison groups.
The set of outputs a function produces over its declared domain.

In this lesson, a single number that measures spread: the largest value in a data set minus the smallest, carrying the same unit as the data. It uses only the two most extreme observations, so one unusual or mistyped value can change it dramatically.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-007 defines range as the set of outputs a function produces over its declared domain, which is a collection of values. The statistical sense used here is a different technical meaning of the same word: one number, the maximum minus the minimum of an observed data set, with the unit of the data. The two senses are bridged in the scene where the term is introduced so a learner meeting both is not left to reconcile them alone.

uses.definition: A numerical scale with a meaningful zero, so ratios of values can have a stable interpretation.

A numerical scale with a meaningful zero standing for none of the quantity, so a ratio between two values has a stable interpretation. Fasting glucose in mg/dL, hours before sleep, and a count of nights all sit here.

alignment.note: Adopts the meaning PREM-QNT-003 already gives the term: a numerical scale whose zero is meaningful, so ratios of values can be interpreted. This lesson adds only that a ratio being arithmetically defined is a separate question from the ratio being clinically informative.

uses.definition: An ordered comparison of two quantities by division.
An exponent written as m/n in lowest terms with n positive. Over the reals, it combines an nth root with an mth power; zero and negative bases need the domain checks stated in the lesson.
The possibility that records described as de-identified could still be linked to a person, especially by combining variables with other information.

A cell-surface receptor with an extracellular ligand-binding region, a single transmembrane segment, and an intracellular region carrying a tyrosine kinase domain. Ligand binding brings two receptors together; the juxtaposed kinase domains phosphorylate one another, which raises their activity and creates phosphorylated sequences on the receptor's own tail that intracellular proteins with SH2 or PTB domains can dock onto. What the cell gains is an assembly point built out of the receptor. The family has more than fifty human members.

A protein that binds a particular signal and, as a consequence of binding it, changes what it does. A cell-surface receptor sits in the membrane with a part outside the cell and a part inside, so that a binding event on the outside becomes a change on the inside. In this lesson the Wnt receptor is a pair of proteins working together, Frizzled with LRP5/6, which is a reminder that one receptor function need not mean one receptor molecule.

A reductional division reduces the number of chromosomes per cell; an equational division does not. Meiosis I is reductional because it separates the two homologs of each pair, taking a cell from 46 chromosomes to 23. Meiosis II is equational because it separates sister chromatids, which lowers the chromatid count while leaving the chromosome count at 23. An ordinary mitotic division is equational in the same sense.
The acute nonnegative angle between a terminal side and the horizontal axis, used with quadrant signs to interpret a standard-position direction.
The whole, baseline, or starting value used as the denominator that gives a ratio or percentage its meaning.

The procedure treated as giving the correct answer while a test is being judged against it. It is the best available comparison for the study at hand and not a guarantee of truth, so a test's reported figures describe its agreement with that particular standard.
A publication format in which a journal evaluates the research question and proposed method before results are known and later evaluates execution, justified changes, and conclusions.

A fitted equation giving an expected value of one measured quantity from one or more others, together with the acknowledgement that individual observations depart from it. In this lesson the fitted part is a straight line, y = a + bx, and the departures are the residuals.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-010 narrowed 'model' from the broad scientific sense to one fitted relationship, y = kx^p, judged by fit, residuals, and assumptions instead of by mechanism. This lesson narrows the word again to a different family of shapes: an additive equation with an intercept and a rate per unit of each predictor. The standard of judgment carries over unchanged, so a learner holding that meaning need only swap the shape, and neither sense claims to explain why anything happens. The concept scene bridges the two where the word first appears here.

uses.definition: A family of methods that describe one measured quantity, the response, in terms of one or more others, the predictors, by fitting a function to observed data. The word carries none of its everyday sense of sliding backwards or deteriorating; it is a historical label for the fitting method. When a paper reports that the authors ran a regression, it means they fitted a relationship of this kind.

Cell death that depends on a dedicated molecular machinery, and which can therefore be delayed or accelerated by a genetic or pharmacological intervention. That modulability is the test: if interfering with a component changes the death, the death was regulated. Regulated cell death includes forms whose end result looks necrotic, so the category is defined by mechanism and not by appearance.

The share of recorded trials in which an event occurred: the count of occurrences divided by the number of trials so far. It is an observed quantity that moves as a record grows, unlike the fixed probability it approaches.
The contribution reliable evidence would make to the specified question, considering the match in exposure, outcome, system, population, dose, and timing.
Consistency of scores or measurements across specified replications, such as occasions, raters, or item samples; its interpretation depends on which sources of variation are included.
The extent to which the information in a piece or line of evidence is credible for what it reports, given its design, measurement, conduct, analysis, and reporting.

alignment.note: Lesson 6 defines reliability as the consistency of a measurement across repeated readings. Here reliability is the broader evidence-appraisal sense: the credibility of a whole line of evidence. A measurement can be reliable in the Lesson 6 sense yet sit inside evidence judged not credible here.

uses.definition: Measurement precision when specified conditions are kept the same, commonly including the procedure, operator, measuring system, location, and a short time interval.
An informative test of a scientific claim using newly collected data, with the relation between original and changed conditions made explicit.
Measurement precision when specified conditions change; a useful reproducibility claim names the changed conditions, such as operator, instrument, laboratory, or day.
The set of choices available when designing, measuring, processing, analyzing, and reporting a study, some of which can change the result.
Confounding that remains after analysis because relevant common causes were unmeasured, measured poorly, or controlled inadequately.

A scatter of the residuals against the predictor, with a reference line at zero. Because the fitted trend has been subtracted away, any remaining pattern is displayed at full height. An arch, a funnel, or an influential point can indicate a specific fault; a shapeless band provides no clear evidence against the fitted form over the observed range but does not prove it uniquely correct.
Observed response minus the response predicted by a model at the same input.

An observed value minus the value the fitted model gives at the same input, in the units of the response. A positive residual means the observation came in above the fitted line, a negative one below it.

alignment.note: PREM-QNT-010 defined a residual as the observed response minus the response predicted by a model at the same input, and this lesson keeps that meaning exactly. Only the fitted shape differs: a straight line here, a power relationship there. The lesson also flags that the everyday clinical sense of 'residual', meaning something left behind in a patient, is unrelated to the vertical distance meant here.

uses.definition: A summary whose value changes little when a small number of extreme observations change. The median and the quartiles are resistant; the mean, the range, and the standard deviation are not. Resistance is a property to choose deliberately, because a summary that ignores a change in the extremes also fails to report one that matters.

The smallest separation at which an instrument or eye distinguishes two spatial features as separate, or the finest spatial detail it resolves. Resolution does not by itself determine detection or localisation: a labelled or high-contrast feature narrower than the resolution limit may still produce a detectable signal, while its width, shape, or nearby neighbours remain unresolved. Resolution belongs to the imaging system and conditions, not to the specimen alone.

A random allocation procedure that adds a prespecified restriction to improve balance or another design property. Blocking can keep group sizes close; stratified randomization applies a separate chance procedure within groups defined by characteristics such as centre, age band, or severity. A restriction can make a later assignment easier to guess, which is a concealment concern rather than proof that chance generation failed.

A transition in G1 beyond which a cell no longer requires external growth-factor signalling and will complete the cycle on its own. Treat it as a real change of state whose position is fuzzy rather than as a line ruled across G1: published estimates of when cells cross it vary widely even within a single cell type, and whether one such universal point exists in G1 has been questioned in the literature.
A cohort assembled from existing records that preserve an earlier exposure followed by a later outcome.
A direction in which the proposed outcome influences the proposed exposure, so the observed association may run opposite to the initial causal story.

The machine that builds a protein by reading a messenger RNA transcript. Bacterial ribosomes and eukaryotic cytoplasmic ribosomes differ enough in structure that a drug can bind one and not the other, which is why some antibacterial drugs leave host cells running.

A distribution whose values crowd towards the low end and thin out slowly towards the high end; its mean is often above its median because high values pull the mean towards the long tail. A lower bound and no stated upper bound do not by themselves force this shape, so skew must be supported by the observed distribution or summaries such as a mean above the median. No normal distribution can reproduce established skew because the normal family has no parameter that permits a lean.

One group's risk subtracted from the other's. It is an absolute measure: it keeps the units of the outcome, so it states how many people per hundred, or per thousand, the comparison moves. When the comparison is an intervention that lowers risk it is usually called the absolute risk reduction.

One group's risk divided by the other's. It is a relative measure: the units cancel, so it states how many times as large one risk is and says nothing about where either started. One minus the ratio is the relative risk reduction.

The probability that a stated outcome occurs in a stated group over a stated period, written as a share of that group. It is a conditional probability with the group named in the condition, and it carries no verdict about harm: a risk of recovery is a risk in this sense. The everyday sense of danger is a different meaning of the word.
Stability of a conclusion across specified plausible changes in assumptions, analytic choices, data, or conditions; the relevant changes must always be named.
The set of all outcomes that a stated chance procedure can produce, with each outcome listed once. Drawing one of sixty study rows at random has a sample space of those sixty rows.

The distribution of the values a statistic would take across repeated samples of a fixed size drawn from the same population. For a sample mean it is centred on the population mean and is narrower than the distribution of the individual observations.

The distribution of an estimate across every sample of a given size that could have been drawn under a stated model. For an unbiased estimator it is centred on the fixed true parameter, not on the estimate from one observed sample, and its spread is the standard error.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-006 owns this term and this lesson keeps its meaning unchanged. This lesson uses it only to distinguish the fixed parameter from the estimates and intervals that vary across repeated samples; it does not centre a hypothetical repeat-study distribution on the observed estimate.

uses.definition: The list or route through which a study can actually reach people — a resident register, an appointment list, the room a recruitment poster hangs in. A sample can at best represent its frame, and a frame can fall short of the target population.

The differences between results computed from different samples drawn the same way from the same population. It arises because each sample contains different individuals, and it is present even when every step of the study was carried out correctly.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-008 defines random error as unpredictable variation across repetitions that contributes imprecision rather than a systematic shift, and lists sampling variation as one of its components alongside unpredictable measurement variation. This lesson uses that same idea narrowed to the sampling component only: the variation produced by drawing different individuals, with measurement held fixed. The word error in the alias sampling error carries no suggestion of a mistake, and the orientation scene says so before the term is used.

uses.definition: The signed length of one vector along a unit direction, calculated with a dot product.
In this lesson, one real numerical value, which may be positive, zero, or negative and has no vector direction.
A multiplicative factor comparing a new linear measure or quantity with its reference value.
The size, duration, resolution, or organizational level at which a model represents a system.

A display with one quantitative variable on each axis and one point per observation, used to ask whether the two measurements are related, whether any relationship is straight or curved, whether the spread of one changes across the other, and whether any point is unusual.
An evidence-building process that frames testable questions, compares explanations with observations, and revises conclusions when the evidence requires it; it is not a single rigid recipe.
A selective representation of a system or process, built to answer a stated question by retaining some relationships and omitting others.

alignment.note: Adopts the established meaning of a model as a purposeful representation of selected features; this lesson applies that meaning specifically to scientific questions, assumptions, domains, and failure tests.

uses.definition: A purposeful representation of selected features and relationships used to explain, predict, or test an idea within stated limits.
A representation of a nonzero number as a coefficient multiplied by an integer power of ten; in normalized form the coefficient has absolute value at least 1 and less than 10.

A transporter that moves phospholipids in both directions across a bilayer without specificity and without ATP, randomising the distribution between the leaflets. Switching one on abolishes an asymmetry the cell has been paying to maintain, which is how exposed phosphatidylserine becomes a signal.

Active transport in which the protein moving the solute uphill spends an ion's electrochemical gradient rather than splitting ATP itself. ATP hydrolysis is coupled to the transport only indirectly, through that gradient, and it happens in a different protein. SGLT1 is the example here: it moves glucose uphill and has no ATP-hydrolysing step, so it keeps working after ATP is gone until the gradient it depends on has run down.

An inhibitory chaperone that keeps separase inactive until the metaphase-to-anaphase transition. It is destroyed by ubiquitination by the APC/C, and its destruction is the last controllable step before cohesin is cut. A checkpoint that wants to stop a division has to act at or before this point.

Distortion produced by how people or items came to be in the groups being compared, rather than by anything done to them afterwards. Steering who enters which arm is the form of it that allocation concealment prevents.
Distortion caused when a rule governing inclusion in a sample or analysis changes the target frequency, association, or comparison.

alignment.note: Generalizes Lesson 5's sense. There selection bias is how people came to be in the compared groups (arm entry, which allocation concealment guards); here it is any inclusion rule for a sample or analysis, including survivorship and attrition. The Lesson 5 form is one case of this broader rule-of-inclusion account.

uses.definition: Result-dependent choice or completeness of outcomes, time points, or analyses reported from within a study that measured or planned more.

The secretion by senescent cells of numerous proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors and proteases into the surrounding tissue. It is why a senescent cell is not a quiet one, and it carries both halves of the senescence account: the arrest constrains tumour development, while sustained secretion contributes to age-related pathology and can make the local environment permissive for cancer.
A comparison of results for the same target question under justified alternative assumptions or analytic choices, used to show how dependent the conclusion is on those choices.
A check of how model output changes when selected inputs, parameters, assumptions, boundaries, or model structure change.

alignment.note: Applies Lesson 9's idea to models specifically: there, varying analytic assumptions to test a conclusion's robustness; here, varying a model's inputs, parameters, or structure to see how its output responds. Same robustness logic, applied to a model.

uses.definition: Among people who have the target condition according to the reference standard, the share whose test is positive: P(test positive given condition present). It divides the true positives by a group defined by the reference standard and describes test performance in the evaluated setting, not the probability that a positive result is correct. The everyday sense of being easily affected is unrelated, and so is the sensitivity analysis of PREM-SCI-009 and PREM-SCI-010, which reruns a result under different assumptions.

The enzyme that cleaves cohesin's RAD21 subunit, opening the ring and allowing sister chromatids to separate. It is held inactive until the metaphase-to-anaphase transition by an inhibitory chaperone, securin. Its action is the irreversible step of a division, which is why it is kept behind two locks rather than one.

The sodium-glucose cotransporter of the small-intestinal brush-border membrane, which carries one glucose molecule inward together with two sodium ions. It is a secondary active transporter: it can concentrate glucose inside the cell above the luminal level, and it does so by spending the sodium electrochemical gradient maintained by the basolateral sodium-potassium ATPase rather than by splitting ATP.

A relative of SGLT1 found in the kidney, whose sodium to glucose coupling ratio is one to one rather than two to one. Used in this lesson only as a real instance of a different coupling stoichiometry, so that the consequence of changing that number is a statement about actual proteins.

A stretch of a newly made protein's own amino-acid sequence that says where the protein should go. The signal sequence for the endoplasmic reticulum is recognised by the signal recognition particle as it emerges from the ribosome, and that recognition diverts the whole ribosome and unfinished chain to the endoplasmic reticulum membrane.

The return of a cell towards its unstimulated state when a signal is withdrawn. Termination is part of what makes a signal informative rather than a switch thrown once, and it is often supplied by the continual turnover of the molecules the signal alters. In the canonical Wnt pathway termination needs nothing new to be built, because the machinery that destroys the output is running at all times and simply resumes its usual effect.

The conversion of a binding event outside a cell into a change inside it. Cell-surface receptors act as signal transducers: they turn an extracellular ligand-binding event into intracellular signals that alter the target cell's behaviour. Transduction is a change of medium rather than a change of message, which is why the word is borrowed from engineering.

A molecule released by one cell whose presence and amount change what another cell does. The everyday sense of a signal, as in a traffic signal or a hand signal, keeps the part that matters: something is sent so that something else will change its behaviour. What biology adds is that the sender and receiver are cells and the message is a molecule, so the message carries no content beyond how much of it there is and where it binds. A signal does not name a state of affairs; the receiving cell's machinery supplies all of the interpretation. Distinct from a signal sequence, which is part of a protein's own chain and addresses the inside of one cell.

A relay chain that contains multiple amplification steps. The definition matters because the word is often applied to any multi-step pathway and the amplification then read back out of the label. Whether a given chain earns the word is a question to answer with evidence about its steps: phototransduction has two identifiable multiplying steps, while the canonical Wnt pathway's identifiable catalytic steps sit on the arm that destroys its output. This is the narrower of two usages. The term is also applied loosely to any multi-step relay, so a source calling a pathway a cascade is not by itself evidence that the pathway amplifies.

A probability chosen before the data are seen, setting how far into the tail of the null distribution a result must fall before the analysis calls the data incompatible with the null. It belongs to the study's design and is conventionally 0.05. It is compared with the p-value and is a separate quantity from it, since one is fixed in advance and the other is measured afterwards.

The cut-off a study fixes in advance for rejecting the null hypothesis, written alpha. Setting it at 0.05 accepts a 5 in 100 chance of rejecting a true null. It is a design decision made before the data arrive and is not adjusted in light of them.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-008 introduces hypothesis testing, the p-value, and the threshold a p-value is compared against, and this lesson keeps that meaning unchanged. What is added here is the reading of the threshold as a rate: the proportion of studies of a true null that would reject it.
