Anything about how a p-value is computed or what it conditions on belongs to the earlier lesson, and this lesson assumes it. The everyday sense of the word describing a result as noteworthy is not used anywhere in this block.

uses.definition: Movement of a solute across a lipid bilayer by dissolving in it and diffusing through, with no protein involved and no energy source beyond the solute's own concentration difference. Available to small nonpolar molecules such as oxygen and carbon dioxide, and much more slowly to small uncharged polar molecules such as water and urea. Ions are effectively excluded.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-002 owns diffusion as the spreading of molecules by random thermal motion with no motor or flow, and that meaning is kept unchanged here. This lesson narrows it to the particular case of that motion carrying a solute across a bilayer unaided, which is one of the four transport routes it classifies. The mean-square-displacement behaviour taught in the earlier lesson still governs the motion; nothing about it is revised.

uses.definition: Random allocation using one fixed allocation ratio for every participant, without blocks, strata, or covariate-adaptive changes to the probabilities. It is the main introductory model in this lesson, not the only valid form of random allocation.
For a right-triangle acute angle, opposite divided by hypotenuse; on the unit circle, the vertical coordinate.

One of the two identical copies of a chromosome produced when S phase replicates it, while the two remain physically attached to each other. Because they are identical, it does not matter which daughter cell receives which; what matters is that each daughter receives exactly one. They are held together by cohesin from S phase until anaphase, and the cutting of that link is the step that commits a cell to finishing its division.

The two identical chromatids produced when one chromosome is replicated, joined at the centromere. Because one was copied from the other they carry the same DNA sequence, which is what distinguishes them from the two homologs of a pair. An ordinary mitotic division separates sister chromatids; meiosis separates them only at its second division.

The protein glue holding sister chromatids together, running along the chromatid arms and also through the centromere. It is one substance in two locations, released in two stages: the arm cohesion at the start of anaphase I, and the centromeric cohesion only at the second division. That staging fixes the order of the two separations, and because the swapped arms beyond a crossover are held by arm cohesion, cutting it is also what lets the chiasma give way. This lesson shortens the name to cohesion where the context is chromosomes; it is unrelated to the cell-to-cell adhesion PREM-BIO-007 treats.

The lack of symmetry in a distribution. A distribution is skewed right when its right tail is long relative to its left, and skewed left when its left tail is longer. A long right tail often lifts the mean above the median and a long left tail often lowers it, but the comparison is not a universal shape test.

The fitted change in the response for a one-unit increase in the predictor, carrying the units of the response divided by the units of the predictor. In this lesson it is −3.37 mg/dL per hour. Its sign depends on the direction the predictor was defined to count, so a slope means nothing until the axis is named.

The ATP-splitting carrier of the plasma membrane that exports three sodium ions and imports two potassium ions for every ATP molecule hydrolysed. In the enterocyte it sits in the basolateral membrane, where it keeps cytosolic sodium low and, by removing one net positive charge per cycle, contributes to holding the cell interior negative. It builds the gradient that every sodium-coupled transporter in the cell then spends.
All values in the declared domain that make an equation true.

Any cell of the body that is not on the path to becoming a gamete. Somatic cells divide mitotically, remain diploid, and never undergo meiosis. Every cell in a colonic crypt is somatic, which is why genetic novelty there is damage rather than product.

Among people who do not have the target condition according to the reference standard, the share whose test is negative: P(test negative given condition absent). It divides the true negatives by a group defined by the reference standard and describes test performance in the evaluated setting. Its complement is the false-positive rate.

The surveillance mechanism that keeps APC/C inactive until the chromosomes are properly attached to the spindle, working through a complex assembled at kinetochores that are not correctly engaged. A single unattached kinetochore is sufficient to sustain the arrest. Two limits matter as much as the mechanism: it is satisfied by a merotelic attachment, which is wrong but presents neither an unattached kinetochore nor an absence of tension, and it gives way after several hours as cyclin B decays.

The apparatus of protein fibres a dividing cell builds to move its chromosomes. It has two ends, called poles, and pulls each chromosome toward one pole or the other. Because one spindle has two poles, one division yields two cells, and that limit is the reason meiosis needs two divisions to reach four products.

The square root of the variance, which returns the spread to the unit of the original data. Read it as roughly the distance a typical observation sits from the mean, in either direction. Because it shares the data's unit, it can be set beside a mean, a group difference, or a measurement precision and compared directly, and dividing a difference by it produces a quantity with no unit at all.

The square root of a distribution's variance, returning its spread to the unit of the values. It can describe any distribution, including a distribution of individual observations or a sampling distribution. The sample standard deviation s describes the observed sample and estimates the population standard deviation sigma; the standard deviation of a statistic's sampling distribution is its standard error.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-003 owns this term and this lesson keeps its meaning exactly. It is restated here only because the whole misconception scene turns on holding it apart from the standard error, and a learner needs both definitions in view at once to do that. Anything about how a standard deviation is computed from the data belongs to the earlier lesson.

uses.definition: The standard deviation of a statistic's sampling distribution, measuring its spread across repeated samples. For a mean of independent observations it is the population standard deviation sigma divided by the square root of n. Because sigma is usually unknown, s divided by the square root of n is reported as an estimated standard error. Comparing two independent means requires combining both standard errors rather than treating one as the spread around the other.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-006 defines measurement error as the difference between a measured value and a reference value, which is the sense in which a mis-calibrated meter produces an error. A standard error contains the same word and reports something else entirely: how far a correctly computed statistic would move if the study were repeated on different people. No measurement is wrong when a standard error is large. The orientation scene names this collision before the term is first used and keeps both senses available.

uses.definition: The standard deviation of an estimate across repeated samples of the same size: how far the study's number would move if the whole study were run again on fresh people. It sets the unit an interval is measured in.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-006 owns this term and its derivation from the sampling distribution, and this lesson keeps that meaning unchanged. Nothing new is added to the definition here; the standard error is taken as an input and turned into the width of an interval. A learner who cannot say what the standard error describes is sent back to that lesson in the opening scene.

uses.definition: The normal distribution with mean 0 and standard deviation 1, which is what any normal measurement becomes once it has been standardised. Because every normal distribution maps onto this one, the same three percentages describe the bands at ±1, ±2 and ±3 for every measurement ever standardised.

Any value computed from the observations in a sample, such as their mean, their standard deviation, or the proportion of them above a cut-point. Because the sample was one of many that could have been drawn, a statistic is a quantity that would come out differently on a repeat.

Comparing observations that already match on one or more recorded variables, so those variables cannot account for the difference being reported. It is arithmetic performed on data already collected, not an intervention, so it reaches only the variables somebody measured and only as well as they were measured.

The full set of assumptions needed to turn a hypothesis into a prediction about data. For the dinner-timing comparison it holds the null value, the treatment of participants as independent contributors, the within-group spread of 16 mg/dL, the shape of the reference curve, and the assumption that the analysis reported was the analysis planned. Every probability in this lesson is computed inside this set, so it inherits every fault the set contains.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-010 defines a scientific model as a selective representation of a system built to answer a stated question, and PREM-SCI-010's term-model-assumption as a simplification accepted so the model can represent selected relationships. This lesson narrows both to the statistical case: the representation is of how data would be generated under a stated hypothesis, and its assumptions are the specific conditions a test's probability calculation relies on. The narrower sense does not replace the broader one, and the assumptions here are model assumptions in exactly PREM-SCI-010's sense.

uses.definition: The property of a test result whose p-value falls at or below a cut-off chosen in advance. The p-value measures how compatible the data are with one specified statistical model, so the label records where a number computed from the data landed relative to a line drawn beforehand. It reports nothing about how large the effect is, nothing about whether the effect would change a decision, and nothing about who would benefit.

alignment.note: PREM-STA-008 introduced the label and its arithmetic. This lesson keeps that meaning exactly and extends it with the disambiguation the learner needs: in ordinary English significant means large enough to matter, and the technical phrase carries no such content. Scene 2 bridges the two senses where the everyday word first appears, and names the second question practical significance so it can be asked separately.

uses.definition: A label applied to a test result whose p-value falls at or below the significance level chosen in advance. It records where one number landed relative to a threshold. In this technical sense the word carries no information about how large an effect is, how important it is, or whether anyone should act on it, which separates it sharply from the everyday sense of significant meaning sizeable or worth attention.
Methods for describing variation in data and reasoning carefully from observations to bounded conclusions.

A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. The definition is about capacity rather than continuous activity: some stem-cell populations are quiescent until activated, while others cycle actively. In this lesson the term names the active stem cells at the crypt base that supply the differentiating cells of the lining. Lessons 08 and 10 of this block develop what division involves and what happens when its control fails.

A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. The definition is about capacity rather than continuous activity: some stem-cell populations are quiescent until activated, while others cycle actively. In this lesson the term names the cells at the crypt base, which are the cells with the highest Wnt activity and whose gene programme this lesson's pathway switches on.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-001 defines stem cell for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration: capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny, with capacity distinguished from continuous division. Nothing is narrowed or extended here. What this lesson adds is the mechanism by which the crypt-base population's programme is switched on, which PREM-BIO-001 deferred to a later lesson in the block.

uses.definition: A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. Capacity is not continuous activity: a human colonic crypt holds between 5 and 10 active stem cells that each divide only about once every two to three days, so most are not dividing at any given moment. They are the slowest-dividing cells in the dividing part of the crypt, and the speed of renewal lives in their amplifying daughters.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-001 defined a stem cell by its capacity to self-renew and produce differentiated progeny, and was explicit that capacity is not continuous activity; PREM-BIO-006 adopted that meaning unchanged and deferred what division involves to this lesson. This lesson keeps the same meaning and nothing is narrowed or extended. What it adds is the division arithmetic lesson one deferred: how many stem cells a crypt holds, how often each divides, and why that rate makes an amplifying compartment arithmetically necessary.

uses.definition: A cell with the capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny. The definition is about capacity rather than continuous activity: some stem-cell populations are quiescent until activated, while others cycle actively. In this lesson the term names the 12 to 16 cells at the base of a colonic crypt whose divisions renew the lining, and every one of those divisions is somatic.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-001 defines stem cell for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration: capacity to self-renew and to produce differentiated progeny, with capacity distinguished from continuous division. Nothing is narrowed or extended, and the definition is not converted into an activity-based one even though this lesson quotes a division interval for the crypt population. PREM-BIO-006 adopted the same sense earlier. What this lesson adds is only that these divisions are somatic and so never meiotic.

uses.definition: A comparison carried out within part of the study population, such as women over 60 or patients above a body mass index cut-point. Subgroups are usually smaller than the whole study, and examining many raises multiplicity concerns. A claim that effects differ between subgroups requires an appropriate interaction analysis, not merely significance in one subgroup and non-significance in another.

An outcome whose value depends on a person's rating, interpretation, or judgement — such as a self-reported score or a clinician's assessment — as opposed to one recorded by an instrument or automatic process. Subjective outcomes are the most exposed to detection bias.

The surface area a body has per unit of its volume, written A/V and carried in reciprocal micrometres for cells. For a sphere of radius r it equals 3/r, so it falls as a cell grows. It decides how much membrane is available to serve each unit of interior.
A selection mechanism in which only cases that remained alive, functioning, successful, persistent, or otherwise observable pass into the analyzed set.

A distribution that looks the same to the left and to the right of its centre point. If the mean exists and the median is unique, both lie at that centre. A mode lies there only with an additional unimodal, single-central-mode condition. Mean-median agreement alone does not establish symmetry and can also occur in skewed or separated data.

A coupled carrier that moves two solutes across a membrane in the same direction, so that the downhill movement of one can drive the uphill movement of the other. SGLT1 is a symporter for sodium and glucose. The broader word cotransporter covers symporters together with antiporters, so it is not interchangeable with this one.
The component of measurement error that remains constant or varies predictably across replicate measurements and appears as a shared shift or pattern relative to an appropriate reference.

A curve shaped like the normal one but with slightly heavier tails, used in place of it when the spread of the data had to be estimated from the same sample as the estimate. Its multipliers are a little larger than the normal ones, and the difference shrinks as the sample grows.
For a right-triangle acute angle, opposite divided by adjacent; equivalently sine divided by cosine where defined.
The whole group whose characteristics a study is meant to describe, as distinct from the smaller group that the study actually enrolled.
The population or complete set of cases about which a stated estimate or conclusion is intended to speak.

alignment.note: Adopts Lesson 5's meaning: the whole group a study is meant to describe, as opposed to the sample actually studied.

uses.definition: The quantity that a measurement is intended to estimate, such as the duration of a specified event.

The layer of cross-linked filaments just beneath the bases of the microvillar core bundles, containing a non-erythrocytic spectrin that ties adjacent bundles to one another as they enter the apical cytoplasm. It is the mat the microvillar rods are planted in, and it is also where keratin anchored at the desmosomes reaches, which makes the apical and lateral cytoskeletons mechanically continuous.

A number computed from the data to measure how far the observation sits from what the model predicts, built so that it grows as the data depart from the hypothesis. In this lesson it is the observed difference minus the null value, divided by the standard error, which expresses the gap in standard errors and so removes the original units. The two-mean worked examples label it z because they use a declared normal approximation; another procedure may use a different reference curve and label.
A question connected to observations or measurements that could produce more than one possible answer within stated boundaries.

Carrying twice the normal complement of chromosomes, as a cell does when it exits mitosis without dividing or when its cytokinesis fails. Two routes in this lesson produce it: mitotic slippage out of a checkpoint arrest, and outright failure of the cleavage. Neither is caught by any checkpoint, and binucleate primary human cells produced by cleavage failure went on to replicate their DNA and re-enter mitosis at close to normal frequency.

In current scientific usage, a broad, coherent and predictive explanatory framework that integrates observations and hypotheses and remains revisable as evidence changes. A hypothesis is a more specific proposition that evidence can evaluate and that may test, extend or apply a theory; the terms are not consecutive rungs in a universal promotion ladder, and usage varies between fields. The everyday sense of a private guess is different and is the sense this lesson sets aside.

alignment.note: No earlier lesson holds a glossary entry for this word, so nothing is being overridden. This lesson adopts PREM-SCI-010's attention to scope, assumptions and evidentiary tests, while making explicit that theory and hypothesis differ in explanatory role and breadth rather than forming a universal promotion ladder. The learner's everyday sense of a guess is named and separated from the scientific usage in prose.

uses.definition: The most apical of the cell-to-cell attachments, and the only one that seals the space between neighbouring cells: at it the intercellular space disappears, and it is the rate-limiting step for movement between cells instead of through them. Built from claudins, occludin and JAM-A, with ZO-1, ZO-2 and ZO-3 scaffolds tying them to actin. Its claudins form charge-selective pores, so it is a regulated gate rather than a plug.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-004 established the tight junction as a fence acting in the outer leaflet of the membrane only, which keeps the apical and basolateral surfaces of one cell different. That sense is adopted here unchanged and is restated in scene 4. This lesson extends it by adding the protein composition and the second, separate job of sealing the route between two cells. The two jobs act at right angles to each other, and neither replaces the other.

uses.definition: Organised biological material made from one or more cell types and the extracellular material associated with them. The mix of cell types, the amount and form of extracellular material, and whether the cells are directly attached vary between tissues. A tissue function may depend on organisation, but it need not be absent from every component cell.

The two ways something can cross an epithelial sheet: through the cells, entering at one face and leaving at the other, or between the cells, past the tight junctions. Glucose absorption in this lesson is transcellular throughout. Water is thought to use both, and claudin-2 and claudin-15 have been identified as molecular components of the paracellular water route.

Movement or permeability through an epithelial cell, across its membranes and interior. It is a property to which an individual cell contributes directly and is distinct from continuous barrier coverage across a tissue.

A protein that binds to DNA or to a DNA-bound partner and changes whether nearby genes are transcribed. TCF and LEF are the transcription factors that beta-catenin partners in this pathway, which is how a concentration outside the cell becomes a change in which genes are read.

A dividing cell descended from a stem cell that undergoes a limited number of further divisions before it stops and differentiates. Amplifying cells are most of a crypt's proliferative compartment and supply nearly all of its output, because the handful of stem cells at the base divide too slowly to do so themselves. They also cycle faster than those stem cells, which inverts the natural assumption that the stem cell is the busiest cell in the tissue.

A small membrane-bounded sac that carries cargo between compartments, or from the trans-Golgi network to a chosen face of the cell surface, and delivers it by fusing with the target membrane. Moving the vesicle and fusing it are separate steps, and they can fail separately.
The degree to which a result can support an inference in a population or setting different from the one in which the study comparison was estimated.

alignment.note: Extends PREM-SCI-005's term-external-validity by naming the specific question of applying a result to a different target population or setting; applicability remains associated with that broader prior term.

uses.definition: Integration of results from approaches selected because their important potential biases differ and are assumed to be largely unrelated.

Trisomy is a diploid genome that has gained one chromosome, written 2N+1; monosomy is one that has lost a chromosome, written 2N-1. A gamete carrying two copies of a chromosome gives a trisomy on fusing with a normal gamete, and one carrying none gives a monosomy. Both are whole-chromosome changes, as distinct from segmental changes in which only pieces of chromosomes are gained or lost.

A numerical axis that begins somewhere other than zero, so that a bar shows only the part of its quantity above the starting value. On a bar chart this breaks the proportionality a reader relies on; on a display that encodes value by position, such as a line chart or scatter plot, a restricted range is defensible if it is clearly stated.

An abnormal proliferation of cells. A benign tumour is defined for this lesson as an abnormal proliferation driven by at least one mutation. This lesson uses the word structurally, for a growth that the renewal loop no longer removes, and does not treat it as a diagnosis or attach any clinical meaning to it.

Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is true: announcing an effect that is not there. Its probability, fixed by the investigator before the study, is the significance level alpha. It names a decision that did not match reality and never a mistake in the conduct of the study.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-006 defines measurement error as the difference between a measured value and an appropriate reference quantity, which is the sense in which a mis-calibrated meter produces an error. A Type I error contains the same word and reports something else entirely: a correctly executed test on honest data reached a decision that happened not to match the world. No measurement is wrong when a Type I error occurs. The orientation scene names this collision in learner prose before either error term is used, and keeps the measurement sense available.

uses.definition: Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is false: missing an effect that is there. Its probability is written beta, and unlike alpha it is not chosen. It depends on the size of the real effect, the sample size, the variability of the measurement, and the threshold, so it has no single value for a study until an effect size is named.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-008 defines random error as unpredictable variation across repetitions that contributes imprecision rather than a systematic shift. That is a property of measurements and samples. A Type II error is a property of a decision rule: the test looked, and concluded nothing was there while something was. Sampling variation is one of the reasons a Type II error happens, so the two ideas are connected, but they are not the same object and this lesson never uses error in the earlier lesson's sense.

uses.definition: A limitation in knowledge about a model, its inputs, parameters, structure, or application that affects confidence in its output.
A carrier that transports a single solute across a membrane and is coupled to nothing else. GLUT2 moving glucose alone is the example in this lesson.
The circle centered at the origin with radius 1; a standard-position angle has endpoint coordinates (cosine, sine) on it.
A vector of magnitude one used to specify a direction or basis axis.
The extent to which a measurement, estimate, or inference supports the intended interpretation for its stated target and conditions.
Differences or fluctuations in the represented system that can be characterized but are not necessarily removed by collecting more information.
A feature or quantity that can take different values or conditions in a comparison.
A recorded characteristic that can take different values across the cases in a dataset, held as one column of the file.

alignment.note: PREM-SCI-003 defines a variable by the job it does in one comparison: the factor set differently, the response recorded, or a condition held alike. This lesson keeps that meaning and widens the frame to any recorded characteristic that differs across cases, whatever role it plays in an argument. A column's role and a column's level of measurement are separate properties, and the first scene names that separation for the learner.

uses.definition: The sum of the squared deviations from the mean divided by one less than the number of observations, for a sample. Squaring removes the signs so the deviations do not cancel, at the cost of leaving the result in squared units, such as mg squared per dL squared for glucose data.

A mathematical object that supports vector addition and multiplication by scalars and can be represented by signed components in a chosen basis; only a nonzero Euclidean vector has a unique direction.

A family of secreted signalling proteins, and in this lesson the signal that reports height in the colonic crypt. Mesenchymal cells near the crypt base secrete them and cells further away do not, so Wnt activity falls progressively up the crypt axis. Wnt proteins carry a lipid modification that makes them hydrophobic, which is required for their secretion and is also what makes their travel through watery extracellular space difficult to explain.

A measurement re-expressed as its distance from the mean of a stated reference distribution, counted in standard deviations: z = (x − μ)/σ. It carries no units, so it compares quantities that share none, and it is unchanged by converting the original measurement between units. It reports distance only; turning it into a probability requires a distributional assumption that has been checked.

The single diploid cell formed when two gametes fuse. Every cell of the resulting body descends from it by ordinary division, which is why a chromosome error present in the zygote is present everywhere while one arising later is confined to a patch.
